stories.title: 🌿 Jérémie 1
summaryBullets: Ce livre contient les paroles de Jérémie, fils de Hilqiya, l’un des prêtres, qui habitait à Anatoth, dans le territoire de Benjamin. (1:1).
L’Eternel lui a parlé la treizième année du règne de Josias, fils d’Amôn et roi de Juda, (1:2).

et sous le règne de Yehoyaqim, fils de Josias, roi de Juda, et jusqu’à la fin de la onzième année du règne de Sédécias, fils de Josias, roi de Juda, jusqu’à la déportation des habitants de Jérusalem au cinquième mois. (1:3).
The word of le SEIGNEUR came to Jeremiah, saying (1:4),
Avant de t’avoir formé dans le sein de ta mère, je t’ai choisi ; et avant ta naissance, je t’ai consacré : je t’ai destiné à être prophète pour les peuples. (1:5).
Then Jeremiah said, "Ah, Lord GOD! Behold, I do not know how to speak, for I am only a youth" (1:6).
Mais l’Eternel me répondit : (1:7).
"Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you," declares le SEIGNEUR (1:8).
Then le SEIGNEUR put out his hand and touched Jeremiah's mouth and said, "Behold, I have put my words in your mouth" (1:9).
"See, I have set you this day over nations and over kingdoms, to pluck up and to break down, to destroy and to overthrow, to build and to plant" (1:10).
And the word of le SEIGNEUR came to Jeremiah, saying, "What do you see?" And he said, "I see an almond branch" (1:11).
Then le SEIGNEUR said, "You have seen well, for I am watching over my word to perform it" (1:12).
Puis l’Eternel m’adressa une seconde fois la parole : Que vois-tu encore ? (1:13).
Et l’Eternel me dit : (1:14).
Car je vais appeler ╵tous les peuples des royaumes du Nord,l’Eternel le déclare. (1:15).
"And I will declare my judgments against them, for all their evil in forsaking me; they have made offerings to other gods and worshiped the works of their own hands" (1:16).
"But you, dress yourself for work; arise, and say to them everything that I command you. Do not be dismayed by them, lest I dismay you before them" (1:17).

Et moi dès aujourd’hui, ╵je fais de toi ╵comme une ville fortifiée,comme un pilier de fer ╵et un rempart de bronze ╵face à tout le pays :face aux rois de Juda, ╵à ses ministres,à ses prêtres et à son peuple. (1:18).
"They will fight against you, but they shall not prevail against you, for I am with you," declares le SEIGNEUR, "to deliver you" (1:19).

translationNotes.note: La double mission de Jérémie : jugement et restauration (1:10).

stories.keyTakeaway: Jérémie est appelé et autorisé comme prophète pour confronter Juda et les nations ; Dieu lui montre la menace du nord et promet de le protéger.

stories.title: 💧 Jérémie 2
summaryBullets: The word of le SEIGNEUR came to Jeremiah, saying (2:1),

Va à Jérusalem et crie à ses oreilles :Voici ce que déclare l’Eternel :Je me souviens de ton amour ╵au temps de ta jeunesse,et comment tu m’aimais ╵au temps où tu étais ╵une jeune mariée,lorsque tu me suivais, ╵à travers le désert,dans une terre inculte. (2:2).
Israel was holy to le SEIGNEUR, the firstfruits of his harvest; all who ate of it incurred guilt, and disaster came upon them, declares le SEIGNEUR (2:3).
Vous, communauté de Jacob,et toutes les familles ╵du peuple d’Israël,écoutez la parole ╵que l’Eternel prononce. (2:4).
"What wrong did your fathers find in me that they went far from me, and went after worthlessness, and became worthless?" (2:5).

They did not say, "Where is le SEIGNEUR who brought us up from le pays d’Égypte, who led us in the wilderness, in a land of deserts and pits, in a land of drought and deep darkness, in a land that none passes through?" (2:6).
God brought them into a plentiful land to enjoy its fruits and its good things, but when they came in, they defiled the land and made God's heritage an abomination (2:7).

The priests did not say, "Where is le SEIGNEUR?" Those who handle the law did not know God; the shepherds transgressed, and the prophets prophesied by Baal and went after things that do not profit (2:8).
"Therefore I still contend with you," declares le SEIGNEUR, "and with your children's children I will contend" (2:9).
"Cross to the coasts of Cyprus and see, or send to Kedar and examine with care; see if there has been such a thing" (2:10).
"Has a nation changed its gods, even though they are no gods? But my people have changed their glory for that which does not profit" (2:11).
"Be appalled, O heavens, at this; be shocked, be utterly desolate," declares le SEIGNEUR (2:12).
"For my people have committed two evils: they have forsaken me, the fountain of living waters, and hewed out cisterns for themselves, broken cisterns that can hold no water" (2:13).
"Is Israel a slave? Is he a homeborn servant? Why then has he become a prey?" (2:14).
The young lions have roared against him; they have roared loudly. They have made his land a waste; his cities are in ruins, without inhabitant (2:15).
Moreover, the men of Memphis and Tahpanhes have shaved the crown of your head (2:16).
"Have you not brought this upon yourself by forsaking le SEIGNEUR your God, when he led you in the way?" (2:17).
Maintenant, que te sert ╵de partir en Egypte,pour aller boire ╵les eaux du Nil ?Et que te sert de prendre ╵la route pour te rendre ╵en Assyrie,pour aller boire ╵les eaux du Fleuve ? (2:18).

Your evil will discipline you, and your apostasy will reprove you. Know and see that it is evil and bitter for you to forsake le SEIGNEUR your God; the fear of me is not in you, declares the Lord GOD of hosts (2:19).
"Long ago you broke your yoke and burst your bonds; you said, 'I will not serve.' For on every high hill and under every green tree you bowed down like a whore" (2:20).
"Yet I planted you a choice vine, wholly of pure seed. How then have you turned degenerate and become a wild vine?" (2:21).
"Though you wash yourself with lye and use much soap, the stain of your guilt is still before me," declares the Lord GOD (2:22).
"How can you say, 'I am not unclean, I have not gone after the Baals'? Look at your way in the valley; know what you have done—a restless young camel running here and there" (2:23).
"A wild donkey used to the wilderness, in her heat sniffing the wind! Who can restrain her lust? None who seek her need weary themselves; in her month they will find her" (2:24).
"Keep your feet from going unshod and your throat from thirst. But you said, 'It is hopeless, for I have loved foreigners, and after them I will go'" (2:25).
Comme un voleur a honte ╵lorsqu’il est découvert,ainsi seront couverts de honte ╵la communauté d’Israël,ses rois et ses ministres,ses prêtres, ses prophètes. (2:26).

They say to a tree, "You are my father," and to a stone, "You gave me birth." For they have turned their back to God and not their face, but in the time of their trouble they say, "Arise and save us!" (2:27).
"But where are your gods that you made for yourself? Let them arise, if they can save you, in your time of trouble; for as many as your cities are your gods, O Judah" (2:28).
"Why do you contend with me? You have all transgressed against me," declares le SEIGNEUR (2:29).
"In vain have I struck your children; they took no correction. Your own sword devoured your prophets like a ravening lion" (2:30).

"And you, O generation, behold the word of le SEIGNEUR. Have I been a wilderness to Israel, or a land of thick darkness? Why then do my people say, 'We are free, we will come no more to you'?" (2:31).
"Can a virgin forget her ornaments, or a bride her attire? Yet my people have forgotten me days without number" (2:32).
"How well you direct your course to seek love! So that even to wicked women you have taught your ways" (2:33).
"Also on your skirts is found the lifeblood of the guiltless poor; you did not find them breaking in. Yet in spite of all these things" (2:34),
you say, "I am innocent; surely his anger has turned from me." Behold, I will bring you to judgment for saying, "I have not sinned" (2:35).
"How much you go about, changing your way! You shall be put to shame by Egypt as you were put to shame by Assyria" (2:36).
From there also you will come away with your hands on your head, for le SEIGNEUR has rejected those in whom you trust, and you will not prosper by them (2:37).

stories.title: 💧 Jérémie 3
summaryBullets: "If a man divorces his wife and she goes from him and becomes another man's wife, will he return to her? Would not that land be greatly polluted? You have played the whore with many lovers; and would you return to me?" declares le SEIGNEUR (3:1).

Lève les yeux, regarde ╵les hauteurs du pays :y a-t-il un endroit ╵où tu ne te sois pas ╵livrée à l’inconduite ?Tu guettais tes amants, assise ╵sur le bord des chemins,comme le Bédouin guette ses victimes ╵dans le désert.Et tu as souillé le payspar tes prostitutions ╵et actes mauvais ! (3:2).
Therefore the showers have been withheld, and the spring rain has not come; yet you have the forehead of a whore; you refuse to be ashamed (3:3).
"Have you not just now called to me, 'My father, you are the friend of my youth'" (3:4)?
"Will he be angry forever, will he be indignant to the end?" Behold, you have spoken, but you have done all the evil that you could (3:5).
L’Eternel me dit au temps du roi Josias : As-tu vu ce qu’a fait Israël-l’infidèle ? Elle qui allait sur toute montagne élevée et sous tout arbre vert pour s’y prostituer. (3:6).
"And I thought, 'After she has done all this she will return to me,' but she did not return, and her treacherous sister Judah saw it" (3:7).

"She saw that for all the adulteries of that faithless one, Israel, I had sent her away with a decree of divorce. Yet her treacherous sister Judah did not fear, but she too went and played the whore" (3:8).
"Because she took her whoredom lightly, she polluted the land, committing adultery with stone and tree" (3:9).
"Yet for all this her treacherous sister Judah did not return to me with her whole heart, but in pretense," declares le SEIGNEUR (3:10).
And le SEIGNEUR said to Jeremiah, "Faithless Israel has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Judah" (3:11).

"Go, and proclaim these words toward the north, and say, 'Return, faithless Israel,' declares le SEIGNEUR. 'I will not look on you in anger, for I am merciful,' declares le SEIGNEUR; 'I will not be angry forever'" (3:12).

"Only acknowledge your guilt, that you rebelled against le SEIGNEUR your God and scattered your favors among foreigners under every green tree, and that you have not obeyed my voice," declares le SEIGNEUR (3:13).
"Return, O faithless children," declares le SEIGNEUR, "for I am your master; I will take you, one from a city and two from a family, and I will bring you to Zion" (3:14).
"And I will give you shepherds after my own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding" (3:15).

Or, quand dans le pays, vous vous serez multipliés – l’Eternel le déclare – oui, lorsque vous aurez proliféré, alors on ne parlera plus du coffre de l’alliance de l’Eternel. On n’y pensera plus et l’on ne s’en souviendra plus. Il ne manquera à personne et l’on n’en fera pas un autre. (3:16).

En ce temps-là, on nommera Jérusalem : « Trône de l’Eternel », et tous les peuples s’assembleront en elle au nom de l’Eternel, oui, à Jérusalem. Ils ne persisteront plus à suivre les penchants de leur cœur obstiné et mauvais. (3:17).
En ces jours-là, la communauté de Juda rejoindra celle d’Israël et, du pays du nord, elles reviendront ensemble vers le pays que j’ai donné en patrimoine à vos ancêtres. (3:18).

"I said, 'How I would set you among my sons, and give you a pleasant land, a heritage most beautiful of all nations.' And I thought you would call me 'My Father,' and would not turn from following me" (3:19).
"Surely, as a treacherous wife leaves her husband, so have you been treacherous to me, O house of Israel," declares le SEIGNEUR (3:20).
A voice is heard on the bare heights, the weeping and pleading of Israel's sons because they have perverted their way; they have forgotten le SEIGNEUR their God (3:21).
"Return, O faithless sons; I will heal your faithlessness." "Behold, we come to you, for you are le SEIGNEUR our God" (3:22).
"Truly the hills are a delusion, the orgies on the mountains. Truly in le SEIGNEUR our God is the salvation of Israel" (3:23).
"But the shameful thing has devoured all for which our fathers labored, from our youth—their flocks and their herds, their sons and their daughters" (3:24).

"Let us lie down in our shame, and let our dishonor cover us. For we have sinned against le SEIGNEUR our God, we and our fathers, from our youth even to this day, and we have not obeyed the voice of le SEIGNEUR our God" (3:25).

stories.title: 🧭 Jérémie 4
summaryBullets: "If you return, O Israel," declares le SEIGNEUR, "to me you should return. If you remove your detestable things from my presence, and do not waver" (4:1),
"and if you swear, 'As le SEIGNEUR lives,' in truth, in justice, and in righteousness, then nations shall bless themselves in him, and in him shall they glory" (4:2).
For thus says le SEIGNEUR to the men of Judah and Jerusalem: "Break up your fallow ground, and sow not among thorns" (4:3).

"Circumcise yourselves to le SEIGNEUR; remove the foreskin of your hearts, O men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem; lest my wrath go forth like fire, and burn with none to quench it, because of the evil of your deeds" (4:4).
"Declare in Judah, and proclaim in Jerusalem, and say, 'Blow the trumpet through the land; cry aloud and say, "Assemble, and let us go into the fortified cities!"'" (4:5).
"Raise a standard toward Zion, flee for safety, stay not, for I bring disaster from the north, and great destruction" (4:6).
Un lion surgit de son fourré,celui qui détruit les nations ╵s’est mis en route,il sort de son repairepour ravager votre pays,pour dévaster vos villeset les laisser sans habitants. (4:7).
For this put on sackcloth, lament and wail, for the fierce anger of le SEIGNEUR has not turned back from us (4:8).
Et il arrivera en ce jour-là,l’Eternel le déclare,que le roi perdra tout courage ╵et les ministres avec lui ;les prêtres seront consternéset les prophètes stupéfaits. (4:9).
Then I said, "Ah, Lord GOD, surely you have utterly deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying, 'It shall be well with you,' whereas the sword has reached their very life" (4:10).

En ce temps-là, ╵on dira à ce peuple ╵et à Jérusalem :« Des hauteurs du désert, ╵arrive un vent torride,il vient en direction ╵des membres de mon peuple.Ce vent n’est destiné ╵ni à vanner le blé ╵ni à le nettoyer. (4:11).
"a wind too full for this comes for me. Now it is I who speak in judgment upon them" (4:12).
"Behold, he comes up like clouds; his chariots like the whirlwind; his horses are swifter than eagles—woe to us, for we are ruined!" (4:13).
"O Jerusalem, wash the evil from your heart, that you may be saved. How long shall your wicked thoughts lodge within you?" (4:14).
For a voice declares from Dan and proclaims trouble from Mount Ephraim (4:15).
"Warn the nations that he is coming; announce to Jerusalem, 'Besiegers come from a distant land; they shout against the cities of Judah'" (4:16).
"Like keepers of a field are they against her all around, because she has rebelled against me," declares le SEIGNEUR (4:17).
"Your ways and your deeds have brought this upon you. This is your doom, and it is bitter; it has reached your very heart" (4:18).
"My anguish, my anguish! I writhe in pain! Oh the walls of my heart! My heart is beating wildly; I cannot keep silent, for I hear the sound of the trumpet, the alarm of war" (4:19).
Crash follows crash; the whole land is laid waste. Suddenly my tents are laid waste, my curtains in a moment (4:20).
"How long must I see the standard and hear the sound of the trumpet?" (4:21).
"For my people are foolish; they know me not; they are stupid children; they have no understanding. They are 'wise'—in doing evil! But how to do good they know not" (4:22).
I looked at the earth, and behold, it was without form and void; and at the heavens, and they had no light (4:23).
I looked at the mountains, and behold, they were quaking, and all the hills moved to and fro (4:24).
Je regarde, et voicique l’homme a disparuet les oiseaux se sont enfuis. (4:25).
I looked, and behold, the fruitful land was a desert, and all its cities were laid in ruins before le SEIGNEUR, before his fierce anger (4:26).
For thus says le SEIGNEUR, "The whole land shall be a desolation; yet I will not make a full end" (4:27).
For this the earth shall mourn, and the heavens above be dark; for I have spoken, I have purposed; I have not relented, nor will I turn back (4:28).
At the noise of horseman and archer every city takes to flight; they enter thickets, they climb among rocks. All the cities are forsaken, and no man dwells in them (4:29).

And you, O desolate one, what do you mean that you dress in scarlet, that you adorn yourself with ornaments of gold, that you enlarge your eyes with paint? In vain you beautify yourself; your lovers despise you; they seek your life (4:30).

For I heard a cry as of a woman in labor, anguish as of one giving birth to her first child, the cry of the daughter of Zion gasping for breath, stretching out her hands: "Woe is me! I am fainting before murderers" (4:31).

translationNotes.note: Verbe clé de l'alliance pour la repentance en 3:12-14.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: הִמּוֹלוּ… וְהָסִירוּ עָרְלוֹת לְבַבְכֶם (himmōlu… ve-hāsīru ʿorlot levavkhem) — Greek: περιτμήθητε… ἀφελεῖτε τὰς ἀκροβυστίας τῆς καρδίας — Aramaic: אִתְגְּזֹרוּ… סַקּוּ עָרְלָא דְלִבְכֹון
translationNotes.note: Figure pour ôter la dureté intérieure (4:4).

translationNotes.note: Expression du chaos de la création réutilisée pour dépeindre la dévastation de Juda (4:23).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מִצָּפוֹן (mi-ṣāfōn) — Greek: ἀπὸ βορρᾶ — Aramaic: מן צפונא

stories.title: 🔎 Jérémie 5
summaryBullets: "Run to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem, look and take note! Search her squares to see if you can find a man, one who does justice and seeks truth, that I may pardon her" (5:1).
Though they say, "As le SEIGNEUR lives," they swear falsely (5:2).

O LORD, do not your eyes look for truth? You have struck them down, but they felt no anguish; you have consumed them, but they refused to take correction. They have made their faces harder than rock; they have refused to repent (5:3).
Then I said, "These are only the poor; they have no sense; for they do not know the way of le SEIGNEUR, the justice of their God" (5:4).
"I will go to the great and will speak to them, for they know the way of le SEIGNEUR, the justice of their God." But they all alike had broken the yoke; they had burst the bonds (5:5).

C’est pourquoi surgira ╵le lion de la forêt, ╵il les attaqueraet le loup de la steppe ╵viendra les ravager ;la panthère est tapie ╵près de leurs villes,et tous ceux qui en sortiront ╵se feront déchirer.Parce que leurs péchés ╵se sont multipliés,et que leurs infidélités ╵ne cessent de s’accroître. (5:6).

Avec cela ╵pourrais-je encore ╵te pardonner ?Tes enfants m’ont abandonnéet ils prêtent serment ╵par ce qui n’est pas Dieu.Moi, je les ai comblés ╵et ils sont adultères ;ils vont en foule ╵aux maisons des prostituées. (5:7).
They were well-fed, lusty stallions, each neighing for his neighbor's wife (5:8).
"Shall I not punish them for these things?" declares le SEIGNEUR; "and shall I not avenge myself on a nation such as this?" (5:9).
"Go up through her vine rows and destroy, but make not a full end; strip away her branches, for they are not le SEIGNEUR's" (5:10).
Car le royaume d’Israël ╵et celui de Juda ╵m’ont bien trahi,l’Eternel le déclare. (5:11).
They have spoken falsely of le SEIGNEUR and have said, "He will do nothing; no disaster will come upon us, nor shall we see sword or famine" (5:12).
The prophets will become wind; the word is not in them. Thus shall it be done to them! (5:13).

Therefore thus says le SEIGNEUR, the God of hosts: "Because you have spoken this word, behold, I am making my words in your mouth a fire, and this people wood, and the fire shall consume them" (5:14).

"Behold, I am bringing against you a nation from afar, O house of Israel," declares le SEIGNEUR. "It is an enduring nation; it is an ancient nation, a nation whose language you do not know, nor can you understand what they say" (5:15).
Their quiver is like an open tomb; they are all mighty warriors (5:16).

They shall eat up your harvest and your food; they shall eat up your sons and your daughters; they shall eat up your flocks and your herds; they shall eat up your vines and your fig trees; your fortified cities in which you trust they shall beat down with the sword (5:17).
"But even in those days," declares le SEIGNEUR, "I will not make a full end of you" (5:18).

Et lorsque vous direz : « Pourquoi donc l’Eternel notre Dieu nous traite-t-il ainsi ? », toi, tu leur répondras : « C’est parce que vous m’avez délaissé et que vous avez adoré des divinités étrangères dans votre pays même. Voilà pourquoi vous servirez des étrangers sur un sol qui n’est pas le vôtre. » (5:19).
"Declare this in the house of Jacob; proclaim it in Judah" (5:20):
"Hear this, O foolish and senseless people, who have eyes, but see not, who have ears, but hear not" (5:21).

"Do you not fear me?" declares le SEIGNEUR. "Do you not tremble before me? I placed the sand as the boundary for the sea, a perpetual barrier that it cannot pass; though the waves toss, they cannot prevail; though they roar, they cannot pass over it" (5:22).
"But this people has a stubborn and rebellious heart; they have turned aside and gone away" (5:23).

ils ne disent pas dans leur cœur :« Craignons l’Eternel, notre Dieu,il nous donne les pluies, ╵chacune en sa saison,les pluies d’automne ╵et celles du printemps.C’est lui qui nous réserve ╵les semaines fixées ╵pour faire la moisson. » (5:24).
Your iniquities have turned these away, and your sins have kept good from you (5:25).
For wicked men are found among my people; they lurk like fowlers lying in wait. They set a trap; they catch men (5:26).
Like a cage full of birds, their houses are full of deceit; therefore they have become great and rich (5:27).
Ils sont bien gros et gras,ils battent le record du mal,ils ne rendent pas la justice, ╵ils ne font pas justice à l’orphelin,et ils prospèrent :non, ils ne rendent pas justice aux pauvres. (5:28).
"Shall I not punish them for these things?" declares le SEIGNEUR, "and shall I not avenge myself on a nation such as this?" (5:29).
An appalling and horrible thing has happened in the land (5:30):
the prophets prophesy falsely, and le prêtres rule at their direction; my people love to have it so, but what will you do when the end comes? (5:31).
crossRefs: Deutéronome 28:49-52 — Une nation lointaine comme malédiction de l'alliance.
Amos 5:14-15 — Recherchez le bien, non le mal (justice et vérité).
Michée 3:5-11 — Prophètes et dirigeants corrompus par le gain.

translationNotes.term: Ne pas faire une destruction totale
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לֹא עָשָׂה כָלָה (lo ʿasah kalah) — Greek (LXX): οὐ ποιήσω συντέλειαν — Aramaic (Tg./Syr.): לָא אֶעֱבֵיד כָּלָה
translationNotes.note: Refrain de jugement limité (5:10-18).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: נִבְּאוּ בַשֶּׁקֶר (nibbeʾu ba-sheqer) — Greek (LXX): ἐπροφήτευσαν ἐν ψεύδει — Aramaic: אתנביוּ בכזבא
translationNotes.note: Accusation contre les prophètes qui transmettent de faux messages (5:31).

translationNotes.term: Les prêtres gouvernent de leur propre autorité
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: וְהַכֹּהֲנִים יִרְדּוּ עַל־יְדֵיהֶם (ha-kohanim yirdū ʿal-yedehem) — Greek (LXX): οἱ ἱερεῖς ἐπικρατοῦσιν διὰ χειρῶν — Aramaic: כַּהֲנַיָּא שולְטִין בִּידֵיהוֹן
translationNotes.note: Expression idiomatique : les prêtres exercent le pouvoir « par leurs mains », c'est-à-dire de leur propre initiative (5:31).

stories.keyTakeaway: Jérusalem est mise à nu comme corrompue de haut en bas ; le jugement arrive par une nation étrangère, mais sans anéantissement total.

stories.title: 📣 Jérémie 6
summaryBullets: Fuyez, Benjaminites, ╵quittez Jérusalem ! (6:1).
The lovely and delicate one, the daughter of Zion, I will destroy (6:2).
Shepherds with their flocks shall come against her; they shall pitch their tents around her; they shall pasture, each in his place (6:3).
Préparez-vous ╵pour le combat contre elle !Debout ! Donnons l’assaut ╵à l’heure de midi !Hélas, malheur à nous ╵car, déjà, le jour baisse,et les ombres du soir s’allongent… (6:4).
"Arise, and let us attack by night and destroy her palaces!" (6:5).
For thus says le SEIGNEUR of hosts: "Cut down her trees; cast up a siege mound against Jerusalem. This is the city that must be punished; there is nothing but oppression within her" (6:6).
As a well keeps its water fresh, so she keeps fresh her evil; violence and destruction are heard within her; sickness and wounds are ever before me (6:7).
"Be warned, O Jerusalem, lest I turn from you in disgust, lest I make you a desolation, an uninhabited land" (6:8).
Thus says le SEIGNEUR of hosts: "They shall glean thoroughly as a vine the remnant of Israel; like a grape gatherer pass your hand again over its branches" (6:9).

To whom shall I speak and give warning, that they may hear? Behold, their ears are uncircumcised, they cannot listen; behold, the word of le SEIGNEUR is to them an object of scorn; they take no pleasure in it (6:10).
Mais moi, je suis rempli ╵de la fureur de Dieu,je ne peux plus la contenir. (6:11).
Leurs maisons passeront à d’autresainsi que leurs champs et leurs femmes,car ma main s’abattra ╵sur les habitants du pays,l’Eternel le déclare. (6:12).
Car tous, petits ou grands,sont avides de gains.Tous, du prophète au prêtre,pratiquent la duplicité. (6:13).
They have healed the wound of my people lightly, saying, "Peace, peace," when there is no peace (6:14).

Sont-ils honteux ╵d’avoir commis ╵des abominations ?Ils n’ont aucune honteet ils ne savent pas rougir,et c’est pourquoi ils tomberont ╵avec ceux qui succombent,et ils s’écrouleront ╵au moment où je leur ferai ╵rendre des comptes,l’Eternel le déclare. (6:15).

Thus says le SEIGNEUR: "Stand by the roads, and look, and ask for the ancient paths, where the good way is; and walk in it, and find rest for your souls. But they said, 'We will not walk in it'" (6:16).
Alors j’ai établi ╵des sentinelles parmi vous ╵qui vous ont dit :« Prêtez donc attention ╵au son du cor ! »Mais ils ont répondu :« Nous n’écouterons pas » ! (6:17).
Therefore hear, O nations, and know, O congregation, what will happen to them (6:18).
Hear, O earth; behold, I am bringing disaster upon this people, the fruit of their devices, because they have not paid attention to my words; and as for my law, they have rejected it (6:19).
"What use to me is frankincense that comes from Sheba, or sweet cane from a distant land? Your holocaustes are not acceptable, nor your sacrifices pleasing to me" (6:20).
Therefore thus says le SEIGNEUR: "Behold, I will lay before this people stumbling blocks against which they shall stumble; fathers and sons together, neighbor and friend shall perish" (6:21).
Voici ce que déclare l’Eternel :« Un peuple va venir de la contrée du nord,une grande nation ╵qui se met en campagne ╵des confins de la terre. (6:22).

They lay hold on bow and javelin; they are cruel and have no mercy; the sound of them is like the roaring sea; they ride on horses, set in array as a man for battle, against you, O daughter of Zion! (6:23).
"We have heard the report of it; our hands fall helpless; anguish has taken hold of us, pain as of a woman in labor" (6:24).
"Go not out into the field, nor walk on the road, for the enemy has a sword; terror is on every side" (6:25).
O daughter of my people, put on sackcloth, and roll in ashes; make mourning as for an only son, most bitter lamentation, for suddenly the destroyer will come upon us (6:26).
"I have made you a tester of metals among my people, that you may know and test their ways" (6:27).
They are all stubbornly rebellious, going about with slanders; they are bronze and iron; they all act corruptly (6:28).
The bellows blow fiercely; the lead is consumed by the fire; in vain the refining goes on, for the wicked are not removed (6:29).
Rejected silver they are called, for le SEIGNEUR has rejected them (6:30).
crossRefs: Ésaïe 1:11-17 — Sacrifices rejetés sans la justice.
Ézéchiel 13:10 — Crépi et fausse paix.
Deutéronome 20:19-20 — Arbres lors d'un siège (contexte sur l'abattage des arbres).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: נְתִיבוֹת עוֹלָם / דֶּרֶךְ הַטּוֹב (netivot ʿolam / derekh ha-tov) — Greek (LXX): τρίβοι αἰώνιοι / ὁδὸς ἀγαθή — Aramaic: שבילֵי עָלְמָא / אורח טב
translationNotes.note: Appel à revenir aux voies anciennes et établies de la fidélité à l'alliance (6:16).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שָׁלוֹם שָׁלוֹם (shalom shalom) — Greek (LXX): εἰρήνη εἰρήνη — Aramaic: שלמא שלמא
translationNotes.note: Fausse assurance que tout va bien (6:14).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כֶּסֶף נִמְאָס (kesef nimʾas) — Greek (LXX): ἀργύριον ἀπώσθη — Aramaic: כספא מסיא
translationNotes.note: Image de la fonderie : le minerai ne produit aucun vrai métal ; le peuple refuse d'être purifié (6:30).

stories.keyTakeaway: Juda refuse le bon chemin et couvre la pourriture d'une fausse « paix ». Un siège du nord approche ; Dieu rejette le culte vide.

stories.title: 🕍 Jérémie 7
summaryBullets: Voici ce que l’Eternel dit à Jérémie : (7:1).
"Hear the word of le SEIGNEUR, all you men of Judah who enter these gates to worship le SEIGNEUR" (7:2).
Thus says le SEIGNEUR of hosts, the God of Israel: "Amend your ways and your deeds, and I will let you dwell in this place" (7:3).
"Do not trust in these deceptive words: 'This is the temple of le SEIGNEUR, the temple of le SEIGNEUR, the temple of le SEIGNEUR'" (7:4).
"For if you truly amend your ways and your deeds, if you truly execute justice one with another" (7:5),
"if you do not oppress the sojourner, the fatherless, or the widow, or shed innocent blood in this place, and if you do not go after other gods to your own harm" (7:6),
"then I will let you dwell in this place, in the land that I gave of old to your fathers forever" (7:7).
"Behold, you trust in deceptive words to no avail" (7:8).
"Will you steal, murder, commit adultery, swear falsely, make offerings to Baal, and go after other gods that you have not known" (7:9),
"and then come and stand before me in this house, which is called by my name, and say, 'We are delivered!'—only to go on doing all these abominations?" (7:10).
"Has this house, which is called by my name, become a den of robbers in your eyes? Behold, I myself have seen it," declares le SEIGNEUR (7:11).
"Go now to my place that was in Shiloh, where I made my name dwell at first, and see what I did to it because of the evil of my people Israel" (7:12).
"And now, because you have done all these things," declares le SEIGNEUR, "and when I spoke to you persistently you did not listen, and when I called you, you did not answer" (7:13),
ce temple qui m’appartient, et sur lequel vous fondez votre assurance, ce lieu que j’ai donné à vous et à vos ancêtres, je vais le traiter de la même manière que j’ai traité Silo. (7:14).
"And I will cast you out of my sight, as I cast out all your kinsmen, all the offspring of Ephraim" (7:15).
"As for you, do not pray for this people, or lift up a cry or prayer for them, and do not intercede with me, for I will not hear you" (7:16).
Ne vois-tu pas tout ce qu’ils font dans les villes de Juda, et dans les rues de Jérusalem ? (7:17).

Les enfants ramassent du bois, les pères allument le feu, les femmes pétrissent la pâte pour faire des gâteaux pour la Reine du ciel. On offre des libations à des dieux étrangers et tout cela m’irrite. (7:18).
"Is it I whom they provoke?" declares le SEIGNEUR. "Is it not themselves, to their own shame?" (7:19).

C’est pourquoi, voici ce que déclare le Seigneur, l’Eternel : Mon ardente colère et mon indignation vont fondre sur ce lieu, sur les gens et les bêtes, sur les arbres des champs et les produits du sol. Et elles brûlent comme un feu qui ne s’éteindra pas. (7:20).
Thus says le SEIGNEUR of hosts, the God of Israel: "Add your holocaustes to your sacrifices, and eat the flesh" (7:21).
"For in the day that I brought them out of le pays d’Égypte, I did not speak to your fathers or command them concerning holocaustes and sacrifices" (7:22).
"But this command I gave them: 'Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and you shall be my people. And walk in all the way that I command you, that it may be well with you'" (7:23).
But they did not obey or incline their ear, but walked in their own counsels and the stubbornness of their evil hearts, and went backward and not forward (7:24).
From the day that your fathers came out of le pays d’Égypte to this day, I have persistently sent all my servants the prophets to them, day after day (7:25).
Yet they did not listen to me or incline their ear, but stiffened their neck. They did worse than their fathers (7:26).
Dis-leur toutes ces choses, mais ils ne t’écouteront pas ; appelle-les, mais ils ne te répondront pas. (7:27).
"And you shall say to them, 'This is the nation that did not obey the voice of le SEIGNEUR their God, and did not accept discipline. Truth has perished; it is cut off from their lips'" (7:28).
"Cut off your hair and cast it away; raise a lamentation on the bare heights, for le SEIGNEUR has rejected and forsaken the generation of his wrath" (7:29).
"For les fils de Judah have done evil in my sight," declares le SEIGNEUR. "They have set their detestable things in the house that is called by my name, to defile it" (7:30).

Ils ont érigé les hauts lieux de Topheth dans la vallée de Ben-Hinnom, afin de brûler leurs fils et leurs filles pour les offrir en sacrifices. C’est bien là quelque chose que je n’ai pas ordonné et qui ne m’est même pas venu à la pensée. (7:31).

C’est pourquoi, le temps vient – l’Eternel le déclare – où l’on ne dira plus : « le Topheth » ni « la vallée de Ben-Hinnom » mais on l’appellera : « la vallée du Massacre », et faute de place, on enterrera les morts au Topheth. (7:32).
Les cadavres des gens de ce peuple serviront de pâture aux oiseaux et aux bêtes sauvages, sans que personne les chasse. (7:33).
Je ferai cesser dans les villes de Juda et dans les rues de Jérusalem les cris de réjouissance et d’allégresse, la voix du marié et la voix de la mariée, car le pays sera en ruine. (7:34).
crossRefs: 1 Samuel 4:10-11 ; Psaume 78:60-61 — La perte de l'arche à Silo et son abandon.
Matthieu 21:13 — « Repaire de brigands » cité plus tard au sujet du temple.
2 Rois 23:10 — Topheth souillé par Josias ; pratique condamnée.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מְעָרַת פָּרִצִים (meʿarat paritsim) — Greek (LXX): σπήλαιον λῃστῶν — Aramaic: מערתא דמרדין
translationNotes.note: Non pas un lieu de justice, mais une cachette pour des malfaiteurs violents (7:11).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מְלֶכֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם (meleket ha-shamayim) — Greek (LXX): βασίλισσα τοῦ οὐρανοῦ — Aramaic: מלכתא דשמיא
translationNotes.note: Titre lié à une idolâtrie populaire (7:18).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: תֹּפֶת / גֵּי בֶן־הִנֹּם (Topheth / Ge Ben-Hinnom) — Greek (LXX): Τοφέθ / φάραγξ υἱοῦ Ἑννόμ — Aramaic: תפת / גֵּיא בן הינום
translationNotes.note: Lieu de sacrifice d'enfants ; associé plus tard à l'imagerie de la « Géhenne » (7:31-32).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: דָּם נָקִי (dam naqi) — Greek (LXX): αἷμα ἀθῷον — Aramaic: דם נקי
translationNotes.note: Le sang versé de ceux qui ne sont pas coupables d'un crime capital (7:6).

stories.keyTakeaway: La présence du temple ne protège pas du jugement. Silo est l'avertissement ; l'idolâtrie et le sacrifice d'enfants à Topheth entraîneront la disgrâce.

stories.title: 🕍 Jérémie 8
summaryBullets: A ce moment-là, l’Eternel le déclare, on sortira de leurs tombeaux les ossements des rois de Juda, ceux de ses ministres, ceux des prêtres, ceux des prophètes et ceux des habitants de Jérusalem. (8:1).

On les exposera face au soleil, à la lune et à tous les astres du ciel, ces astres qu’ils ont adorés, auxquels ils ont rendu un culte, qu’ils ont suivis, qu’ils ont consultés et devant lesquels ils se sont prosternés. Ces ossements ne seront pas recueillis de nouveau pour être ensevelis ; ils deviendront du fumier sur le sol. (8:2).
"Death shall be preferred to life by all the remnant that remains of this evil family in all the places where I have driven them," declares le SEIGNEUR of hosts (8:3).
"You shall say to them, Thus says le SEIGNEUR: When men fall, do they not rise again? If one turns away, does he not return?" (8:4).
"Why then has this people turned away in perpetual backsliding? They hold fast to deceit; they refuse to return" (8:5).

I have paid attention and listened, but they have not spoken rightly; no man relents of his evil, saying, "What have I done?" Everyone turns to his own course, like a horse plunging headlong into battle (8:6).

La cigogne elle-même, ╵dans le ciel, connaît bien ╵le temps des migrations,la colombe, la grue ╵et l’hirondelleobservent l’époque de leur retour ;mais mon peuple ne connaît pas ╵les lois que l’Eternel a établies. (8:7).
Comment pouvez-vous dire :« Nous, nous sommes des sageset nous avons la Loi de l’Eternel » ?Car, en réalité, ╵le stylet mensonger ╵des spécialistes de la Loil’a changée en mensonge. (8:8).
Les sages sont couverts de honte,ils sont pris de terreur ╵et emmenés captifs,car ils ont rejeté ╵la parole de l’Eternel.Que peuvent-ils encore ╵avoir comme sagesse ? (8:9).

Aussi, je donnerai ╵à d’autres leurs épouses,et les champs qu’ils cultivent ╵à ceux qui les prendront,car tous, petits et grands,sont avides de gains,tous, du prophète au prêtrepratiquent la duplicité. (8:10).
They have healed the wound of the daughter of my people lightly, saying, "Peace, peace," when there is no peace (8:11).

Sont-ils honteux ╵d’avoir commis ╵des abominations ?Ils n’ont aucune honte,et ils ne savent pas rougir,et c’est pourquoi ils tomberont ╵avec ceux qui succombentet ils s’écrouleront ╵au moment où je leur ferai ╵rendre des comptes,l’Eternel le déclare. (8:12).
"When I would gather them," declares le SEIGNEUR, "there are no grapes on the vine, nor figs on the fig tree; even the leaves are withered, and what I gave them has passed away from them" (8:13).

"Why do we sit still? Gather together; let us go into the fortified cities and perish there, for le SEIGNEUR our God has doomed us to perish and has given us poisoned water to drink, because we have sinned against le SEIGNEUR" (8:14).
We looked for peace, but no good came; for a time of healing, but behold, terror (8:15).

On entend depuis Dan ╵les chevaux qui hennissent.En entendant hennir ╵les fougueux étalons,toute la terre tremble.Les voici, ils arrivent, ╵dévorant le payset tout ce qu’il contient,la ville et tous ses habitants. (8:16).
"For behold, I am sending among you serpents, adders that cannot be charmed, and they shall bite you," declares le SEIGNEUR (8:17).
My joy is gone; grief is upon me; my heart is sick within me (8:18).
La communauté de mon peuple ╵pousse des cris plaintifsdepuis un pays éloigné.L’Eternel, gémit-elle, ╵n’est-il plus en Sion ?Son roi n’est-il plus là ? (8:19).
"The harvest is past, the summer is ended, and we are not saved" (8:20).
Elle est brisée, ╵la communauté de mon peuple, ╵j’en suis brisé,oui, j’en suis accablé, ╵en proie à la consternation. (8:21).
Is there no balm in Gilead? Is there no physician there? Why then has the health of the daughter of my people not been restored? (8:22).

stories.title: 💧 Jérémie 9
summaryBullets: Oh ! que n’ai-je, au désert, ╵un gîte de nomades ! (9:1).
Oh that I had in the desert a travelers' lodging place, that I might leave my people and go away from them! For they are all adulterers, a company of treacherous men (9:2).
They bend their tongue like a bow; falsehood and not truth has grown strong in the land; for they proceed from evil to evil, and they do not know me, declares le SEIGNEUR (9:3).
Let everyone beware of his neighbor, and put no trust in any brother, for every brother is a deceiver, and every neighbor goes about as a slanderer (9:4).
Everyone deceives his neighbor, and no one speaks the truth; they have taught their tongue to speak lies; they weary themselves committing iniquity (9:5).
"You dwell in the midst of deceit; in deceit they refuse to know me," declares le SEIGNEUR (9:6).
Therefore thus says le SEIGNEUR of hosts: "Behold, I will refine them and test them, for what else can I do, because of my people?" (9:7).
Their tongue is a deadly arrow; it speaks deceitfully; with his mouth each speaks peace to his neighbor, but in his heart he plans an ambush (9:8).
"Shall I not punish them for these things?" declares le SEIGNEUR, "and shall I not avenge myself on a nation such as this?" (9:9).
Je ferai de Jérusalem ╵un monceau de décombres,un gîte de chacals ;des villes de Juda, ╵je ferai une terre dévastée,sans habitants. (9:10).
"I will make Jerusalem a heap of ruins, a lair of jackals, and I will make the cities of Judah a desolation, without inhabitant" (9:11).

Who is the man so wise that he can understand this? To whom has the mouth of le SEIGNEUR spoken, that he may declare it? Why is the land ruined and laid waste like a wilderness, so that no one passes through? (9:12).
And le SEIGNEUR says: "Because they have forsaken my law that I set before them, and have not obeyed my voice or walked in accord with it" (9:13),
"but have stubbornly followed their own hearts and have gone after the Baals, as their fathers taught them" (9:14).
Therefore thus says le SEIGNEUR of hosts, the God of Israel: "Behold, I will feed this people with bitter food, and give them poisonous water to drink" (9:15).
"I will scatter them among the nations whom neither they nor their fathers have known, and I will send the sword after them, until I have consumed them" (9:16).
Oui, qu’elles se dépêchent ╵pour prononcer sur nous ╵leurs cris plaintifset que nos yeux fondent en larmeset que les pleurs ruissellent ╵de nos paupières. (9:17).
"Let them make haste and raise a wailing over us, that our eyes may run down with tears and our eyelids flow with water" (9:18).
For a sound of wailing is heard from Zion: "How we are ruined! We are utterly shamed, because we have left the land, because they have cast down our dwellings" (9:19).
« Oh ! la mort a surgi, ╵grimpant par nos fenêtres,pour pénétrer ╵dans nos belles maisonset faire disparaître ╵les enfants de la rueet les jeunes des places. » (9:20).

Proclame-le : ╵Voici ce que déclare l’Eternel :Les cadavres des hommes ╵tomberont sur le solet resteront par terre ╵comme du fumier dans les champs,comme des gerbes ╵que les moissonneurs laissentet que personne ne ramasse. (9:21).
Speak: "Thus declares le SEIGNEUR: 'The dead bodies of men shall fall like dung upon the open field, like sheaves after the reaper, and none shall gather them'" (9:22).
Thus says le SEIGNEUR: "Let not the wise man boast in his wisdom, let not the mighty man boast in his might, let not the rich man boast in his riches" (9:23),

"but let him who boasts boast in this, that he understands and knows me, that Je suis le SEIGNEUR who practices steadfast love, justice, and righteousness in the earth. For in these things I delight," declares le SEIGNEUR (9:24).
"Behold, the days are coming," declares le SEIGNEUR, "when I will punish all those who are circumcised merely in the flesh" (9:25)—

contre les Egyptiens, les Judéens, les Edomites, les Ammonites, les Moabites et tous les habitants des abords du désert qui se rasent le haut des joues, car tous ces peuples ne sont pas vraiment circoncis, et tout le peuple d’Israël a le cœur incirconcis. (9:26).
crossRefs: Psaume 115:4-8 ; Ésaïe 44:9-20 — Idoles qui ne peuvent ni parler ni marcher.
Osée 6:1 — Langage de « guérison » (contraste avec la fausse guérison).
Deutéronome 10:16 — Circoncire le cœur (changement intérieur).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עֵט שֶׁקֶר סֹפְרִים (ʿet sheqer soferim) — Greek (LXX): κάλαμος ψευδής γραμματέων — Aramaic: קולמוסא דכזב דספָרַיָּא
translationNotes.note: Expression indiquant des distorsions écrites ou un maniement trompeur de la loi (8:8).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: צֳרִי (tseri) — Greek (LXX): ῥητίνη/βάλσαμον — Aramaic: צרי
translationNotes.note: Résine curative de Galaad ; posée en question rhétorique sur la vraie guérison (8:22).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: הָלַל (halal, ‘praise/boast’) — Greek (LXX): καυχάομαι — Aramaic: אשתבח
translationNotes.note: La vraie glorification est dirigée vers la connaissance du caractère de Dieu (9:23-24).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֱלִיל/פֶּסֶל… אֵין־רוּחַ (elil/pesel… ein ruaḥ) — Greek (LXX): εἴδωλον… οὐκ ἔστιν πνοή — Aramaic: צלמא… לֵית בֵּיה רוּחָא
translationNotes.note: Contrastée avec le Créateur vivant (10:5) (10:14-16).

stories.title: 💧 Jérémie 10
summaryBullets: Hear the word that le SEIGNEUR speaks to you, O house of Israel (10:1).
Voici ce que déclare l’Eternel :N’adoptez pas ╵la conduite des autres peupleset ne redoutez pas ╵les signes dans le cielmême les peuples étrangers ╵qui les redoutent. (10:2).
Les coutumes des autres peuples ╵sont inutiles,leur dieu n’est que du bois ╵coupé dans la forêt,travaillé au ciseau ╵par la main d’un sculpteur. (10:3).
They decorate it with silver and gold; they fasten it with hammer and nails so that it cannot move (10:4).

Their idols are like scarecrows in a cucumber field, and they cannot speak; they have to be carried, for they cannot walk. Do not be afraid of them, for they cannot do evil, neither is it in them to do good (10:5).
There is none like you, O LORD; you are great, and your name is great in might (10:6).
Qui donc ne te craindrait, ╵ô, roi des peuples ?On doit te craindrecar parmi tous les sages ╵de tous les peupleset dans tous leurs royaumes,nul n’est semblable à toi ! (10:7).
They are both stupid and foolish; the instruction of idols is but wood! (10:8).

C’est de l’argent battu ╵apporté de Tarsis,de l’or venu d’Ouphaz,une œuvre de sculpteur, ╵le travail d’un orfèvre.On revêt ces dieux-là ╵de vêtements de pourpre ╵et d’étoffes d’azur,mais tous ne sont que l’œuvre ╵d’habiles ouvriers. (10:9).
Mais l’Eternel ╵est le vrai Dieu ;il est le Dieu vivant ╵et le roi éternel ;par sa colère, ╵la terre est ébranlée,et les peuples ne peuvent ╵soutenir son courroux. (10:10).
Vous leur direz ceci : Les dieux qui n’ont fait ni le ciel ni la terre disparaîtront de dessus cette terre et de dessous ce ciel. (10:11).
It is he who made the earth by his power, who established the world by his wisdom, and by his understanding stretched out the heavens (10:12).

Quand il fait retentir sa voix,les eaux s’amassent dans le ciel,des nuages s’élèvent ╵des confins de la terre ;il fait jaillir l’éclair ╵au milieu des averseset il fait s’élancer ╵le vent de ses réserves. (10:13).
Every man is stupid and without knowledge; every goldsmith is put to shame by his idols, for his images are false, and there is no breath in them (10:14).
They are worthless, a work of delusion; at the time of their punishment they shall perish (10:15).
Not like these is he who is the portion of Jacob, for he is the one who formed all things, and Israel is la tribu de his inheritance; le SEIGNEUR of hosts is his name (10:16).
Gather up your bundle from the ground, O you who dwell under siege! (10:17).
For thus says le SEIGNEUR: "Behold, I am slinging out the inhabitants of the land at this time, and I will bring distress on them, that they may feel it" (10:18).
Woe is me because of my hurt! My wound is grievous. But I said, "Truly this is an affliction, and I must bear it" (10:19).
My tent is destroyed, and all my cords are broken; my children have gone from me, and they are not; there is no one to spread my tent again and to set up my curtains (10:20).
For the shepherds are stupid and do not inquire of le SEIGNEUR; therefore they have not prospered, and all their flock is scattered (10:21).
Voici ce que déclare l’Eternel :N’adoptez pas ╵la conduite des autres peupleset ne redoutez pas ╵les signes dans le cielmême les peuples étrangers ╵qui les redoutent. (10:22).
I know, O LORD, that the way of man is not in himself, that it is not in man who walks to direct his steps (10:23).
Correct me, O LORD, but in justice; not in your anger, lest you bring me to nothing (10:24).

Pour out your wrath on the nations that know you not, and on the peoples that call not on your name, for they have devoured Jacob; they have devoured him and consumed him, and have laid waste his habitation (10:25).

stories.title: 📜 Jérémie 11
summaryBullets: The word that came to Jeremiah from le SEIGNEUR (11:1):
Ecoutez donc les clauses de cette alliance, tu les énonceras pour les gens de Juda et les habitants de Jérusalem ! (11:2).
"You shall say to them, Thus says le SEIGNEUR, the God of Israel: Cursed be the man who does not hear the words of this covenant" (11:3),

"that I commanded your fathers when I brought them out of le pays d’Égypte, from the iron furnace, saying, Listen to my voice, and do all that I command you. So shall you be my people, and I will be your God" (11:4),
"that I may confirm the oath that I swore to your fathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as at this day." Then I answered, "Amen, LORD" (11:5).
Et l’Eternel me dit : Proclame toutes ces paroles dans les villes de Juda et les rues de Jérusalem ! Dis-leur : Ecoutez les termes de l’alliance, appliquez-les. (11:6).
For I solemnly warned your fathers when I brought them up out of le pays d’Égypte, warning them persistently, even to this day, saying, Obey my voice (11:7).

Yet they did not obey or incline their ear, but everyone walked in the stubbornness of his evil heart. Therefore I brought upon them all the words of this covenant, which I commanded them to do, but they did not (11:8).
L’Eternel ajouta : Les habitants des villes de Juda et de Jérusalem préparent un complot : (11:9).

ils ont commis les mêmes fautes que leurs premiers ancêtres qui avaient refusé d’écouter mes paroles. Eux aussi, ils ont adopté d’autres dieux qu’ils ont adorés ; oui, le royaume d’Israël et le royaume de Juda ont transgressé l’alliance que j’avais autrefois conclue avec leurs ancêtres. (11:10).
Therefore, thus says le SEIGNEUR, "Behold, I am bringing disaster upon them that they cannot escape. Though they cry to me, I will not listen to them" (11:11).

Alors les habitants des villes de Juda et de Jérusalem pourront aller lancer des appels à leurs dieux auxquels ils offrent des parfums. Mais ces dieux-là ne les sauveront pas lorsqu’ils seront dans le malheur. (11:12).
For your gods have become as many as your cities, O Judah, and as many as the streets of Jerusalem are the altars you have set up to shame, altars to make offerings to Baal (11:13).
"Therefore do not pray for this people, or lift up a cry or prayer on their behalf, for I will not listen when they call to me in the time of their trouble" (11:14).
"What right has my beloved in my house, when she has done many vile deeds? Can even sacrificial flesh avert your doom? Can you then exult?" (11:15).
The LORD once called you "a green olive tree, beautiful with good fruit." But with the roar of a great tempest he will set fire to it, and its branches will be consumed (11:16).

Le Seigneur des armées célestes qui t’a planté a décidé ton malheur à cause des méfaits que les gens d’Israël et les gens de Juda ont accomplis, car ils m’ont irrité en offrant des parfums à Baal. (11:17).
The LORD made it known to me and I knew; then you showed me their deeds (11:18).

J’étais comme un agneau docile qu’on mène à l’abattoir et je ne savais pas que c’était contre moi qu’ils concevaient de tels projets, disant : « Abattons l’arbre pendant qu’il est en sève, venez, supprimons-le du monde des vivants, et qu’on ne s’en souvienne plus ! » (11:19).
But, O LORD of hosts, who judges righteously, who tests the heart and the mind, let me see your vengeance upon them, for to you have I committed my cause (11:20).
Therefore thus says le SEIGNEUR concerning the men of Anathoth, who seek your life, and say, "Do not prophesy in the name of le SEIGNEUR, or you will die by our hand" (11:21)—
therefore thus says le SEIGNEUR of hosts: "Behold, I will punish them. The young men shall die by the sword; their sons and their daughters shall die by famine" (11:22),
"and none of them shall be left. For I will bring disaster upon the men of Anathoth, the year of their punishment" (11:23).
crossRefs: Deutéronome 28:1-68 — Bénédictions et malédictions de l'alliance.
Psaume 52:8 ; Romains 11:17 — Imagerie de l'olivier.
Amos 3:7-8 — Le prophète contraint de parler malgré le danger.

translationNotes.term: Ne prie pas pour ce peuple
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אַל־תִּתְפַּלֵּל (ʾal-titpallel) — Greek (LXX): μὴ προσεύχου — Aramaic (Tg./Syr.): לָא תְּצַלֵּי
translationNotes.note: Le jugement a atteint un stade fixé ; cette injonction vise l'intercession de Jérémie, non une interdiction générale de prier pour les gens en tout temps (11:14).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֵזוֹר פִּשְׁתִּים (ʾezor pishtim) — Greek (LXX): ζώνη λινοῦ — Aramaic (Tg.): אֵזוֹר דִּכְתָנָא
translationNotes.note: Un linge de taille ajusté (13:1-11) ; sa détérioration met en scène l'orgueil corrompu de Juda.

translationNotes.term: Couschite (souvent traduit en anglais par « Ethiopian »)
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כֻּשִׁי (Kushi) — Greek (LXX): Αἰθίοψ — Aramaic (Tg./Syr.): כּוּשָׁיָא
translationNotes.note: Ethnonyme pour les habitants de la région de Koush (Nubie/Éthiopie). Le verset utilise un trait permanent de manière proverbiale (13:23), sans être une insulte raciale ni une doctrine d'infériorité.

stories.keyTakeaway: Juda rompt l'alliance, complote pour tuer Jérémie, et est averti par des signes saisissants : l'orgueil pourrira, dirigeants et peuple chancelleront, et l'exil est proche. Pourtant les nations qui apprennent les voies de Dieu peuvent être replantées.

stories.title: 📜 Jérémie 12
summaryBullets: "Righteous are you, O LORD, when I complain to you; yet I would plead my case before you. Why does the way of the wicked prosper? Why do all who are treacherous thrive?" (12:1).
You plant them, and they take root; they grow and produce fruit; you are near in their mouth and far from their heart (12:2).

Mais toi, ô Eternel, ╵tu me connais et tu me vois,et tu sondes mon cœur ╵qui a pris ton parti.Entraîne-les, ╵tout comme des moutons ╵qu’on mène à l’abattoir !Réserve-les, ╵pour le jour du massacre ! (12:3).

Jusques à quand ╵le pays sera-t-il en deuil,et l’herbe des campagnes ╵se desséchera-t-elle ?Et tout cela à cause ╵de la méchanceté ╵de ceux qui y habitent ?Les animaux périssent, ╵ainsi que les oiseaux,parce que les gens disent :« L’Eternel ne voit pas ╵ce qui nous adviendra. »Mais l’Eternel me dit : (12:4).

Si, déjà, tu t’épuisesen courant avec des piétons,comment donc tiendras-tu ╵en courant avec des chevaux ?S’il te faut un pays tranquillepour ta sécurité,qu’adviendra-t-il de toi ╵lorsque tu feras face ╵à la crue du Jourdain ? (12:5).
For even your brothers and the house of your father, even they have dealt treacherously with you; they are in full cry after you; do not believe them, though they speak friendly words to you (12:6).
"I have forsaken my house; I have abandoned my heritage; I have given the beloved of my soul into the hands of her enemies" (12:7).
My heritage has become to me like a lion in the forest; she has lifted up her voice against me; therefore I hate her (12:8).
Is my heritage to me like a hyena's lair? Are the birds of prey against her all around? Go, assemble all the wild beasts; bring them to devour (12:9).
Many shepherds have destroyed my vineyard; they have trampled down my portion; they have made my pleasant portion a desolate wilderness (12:10).
They have made it a desolation; desolate, it mourns to me. The whole land is made desolate, but no man lays it to heart (12:11).
Sur toutes les hauteurs ╵dans le désertarrivent les dévastateurs,car voici que l’épée de l’Eternel ╵ravage le pays ╵d’un bout à l’autre,il n’y a plus de paix ╵pour aucun être humain. (12:12).

Ils ont semé du blé,ils récoltent des ronces ;ils se sont fatigués ╵pour n’aboutir à rien.Le fruit de vos moissons ╵vous remplira de honte,c’est là l’effet de la colère ardente ╵de l’Eternel. (12:13).

Thus says le SEIGNEUR concerning all my evil neighbors who touch the heritage that I have given my people Israel to inherit: "Behold, I will pluck them up from their land, and I will pluck up the house of Judah from among them" (12:14).
And after I have plucked them up, I will again have compassion on them, and I will bring them again each to his heritage and each to his land (12:15).

Et s’ils apprennent à se comporter comme mon peuple, s’ils prêtent serment par mon nom, disant : « L’Eternel est vivant », comme ils ont appris à mon peuple à jurer par Baal, alors ils auront une place au milieu de mon peuple. (12:16).
But if any nation will not listen, then I will utterly pluck it up and destroy it, declares le SEIGNEUR (12:17).

stories.title: 📜 Jérémie 13
summaryBullets: Thus said le SEIGNEUR to me, "Go and buy a linen loincloth and put it around your waist, and do not dip it in water" (13:1).
So I bought a loincloth according to the word of le SEIGNEUR, and put it around my waist (13:2).
And the word of le SEIGNEUR came to me a second time, saying (13:3),
Prends la ceinture que tu as achetée et que tu portes à la taille, et mets-toi en route : va jusqu’au Perath et là, enfouis-la dans une fente de rocher. (13:4).
So I went and hid it by the Euphrates, as le SEIGNEUR commanded me (13:5).
Après bien des jours, l’Eternel me dit : Mets-toi en route, retourne sur les bords du Perath et reprends la ceinture que je t’ai ordonné de cacher là-bas. (13:6).
Je me rendis donc près du Perath, je fouillai, et je pris la ceinture à l’endroit où je l’avais cachée, mais elle était tellement abîmée qu’elle ne pouvait plus servir à rien. (13:7).
Then the word of le SEIGNEUR came to me (13:8):
"Thus says le SEIGNEUR: Even so will I spoil the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem" (13:9).

"This evil people, who refuse to hear my words, who stubbornly follow their own heart and have gone after other gods to serve them and worship them, shall be like this loincloth, which is good for nothing" (13:10).

Car, comme la ceinture est attachée à la taille d’un homme, ainsi je m’étais attaché toute la communauté d’Israël et toute celle de Juda – l’Eternel le déclare – pour qu’elles deviennent pour moi mon peuple et mon honneur, un sujet de louange, une parure. Mais ils ne m’ont pas écouté. (13:11).

Tu leur diras ceci : Voici ce que déclare l’Eternel, le Dieu d’Israël : Toutes les cruches seront remplies de vin. Et ils te répondront : « Ne savons-nous pas que toutes les cruches seront remplies de vin ? » (13:12).

"Then you shall say to them, 'Thus says le SEIGNEUR: Behold, I will fill with drunkenness all the inhabitants of this land: the kings who sit on David's throne, le prêtres, the prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem'" (13:13).
"And I will dash them one against another, fathers and sons together," declares le SEIGNEUR. "I will not pity or spare or have compassion, that I should not destroy them" (13:14).
Hear and give ear; be not proud, for le SEIGNEUR has spoken (13:15).

Give glory to le SEIGNEUR your God before he brings darkness, before your feet stumble on the twilight mountains, and while you look for light he turns it into gloom and makes it deep darkness (13:16).
But if you will not listen, my soul will weep in secret for your pride; my eyes will weep bitterly and run down with tears, because le SEIGNEUR's flock has been taken captive (13:17).
Déclare au roi ╵et à la reine mère :« Asseyez-vous bien bascar le voilà tombé ╵de votre tête,votre superbe diadème. » (13:18).
L’Eternel me parla ainsi : Va t’acheter une ceinture de lin et mets-la autour de la taille, mais ne la mouille pas. (13:19).
"Lift up your eyes and see those who come from the north. Where is the flock that was given you, your beautiful flock?" (13:20).
What will you say when they set as head over you those whom you yourself have taught to be friends to you? Will not pangs take hold of you like those of a woman in labor? (13:21).
And if you say in your heart, "Why have these things come upon me?" it is for the greatness of your iniquity that your skirts are lifted up and you suffer violence (13:22).
Can the Ethiopian change his skin or the leopard his spots? Then also you can do good who are accustomed to do evil (13:23).
"I will scatter you like chaff driven by the wind from the desert" (13:24).
"This is your lot, the portion I have measured out to you," declares le SEIGNEUR, "because you have forgotten me and trusted in lies" (13:25).
"I myself will lift up your skirts over your face, and your shame will be seen" (13:26).
I have seen your abominations, your adulteries and neighings, your lewd whorings, on the hills in the field. Woe to you, O Jerusalem! How long will it be before you are made clean? (13:27).
crossRefs: Deutéronome 28:1-68 — Bénédictions et malédictions de l'alliance.
Psaume 52:8 ; Romains 11:17 — Imagerie de l'olivier.
Amos 3:7-8 — Le prophète contraint de parler malgré le danger.

translationNotes.term: Ne prie pas pour ce peuple
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אַל־תִּתְפַּלֵּל (ʾal-titpallel) — Greek (LXX): μὴ προσεύχου — Aramaic (Tg./Syr.): לָא תְּצַלֵּי
translationNotes.note: Le jugement a atteint un stade fixé ; cette injonction vise l'intercession de Jérémie, non une interdiction générale de prier pour les gens en tout temps (11:14).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אֵזוֹר פִּשְׁתִּים (ʾezor pishtim) — Greek (LXX): ζώνη λινοῦ — Aramaic (Tg.): אֵזוֹר דִּכְתָנָא
translationNotes.note: Un linge de taille ajusté (13:1-11) ; sa détérioration met en scène l'orgueil corrompu de Juda.

translationNotes.term: Couschite (souvent traduit en anglais par « Ethiopian »)
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כֻּשִׁי (Kushi) — Greek (LXX): Αἰθίοψ — Aramaic (Tg./Syr.): כּוּשָׁיָא
translationNotes.note: Ethnonyme pour les habitants de la région de Koush (Nubie/Éthiopie). Le verset utilise un trait permanent de manière proverbiale (13:23), sans être une insulte raciale ni une doctrine d'infériorité.

stories.keyTakeaway: Juda rompt l'alliance, complote pour tuer Jérémie, et est averti par des signes saisissants : l'orgueil pourrira, dirigeants et peuple chancelleront, et l'exil est proche. Pourtant les nations qui apprennent les voies de Dieu peuvent être replantées.

stories.title: 🌵 Jérémie 14
summaryBullets: The word of le SEIGNEUR that came to Jeremiah concerning the drought (14:1):
"Judah mourns, and her gates languish; her people lament on the ground, and the cry of Jerusalem goes up" (14:2).
Her nobles send their servants for water; they come to the cisterns but find no water. They return with their vessels empty; they are ashamed and confounded and cover their heads (14:3).
Le sol est crevassécar la pluie a manqué ╵dans le pays,et les cultivateurs, ╵déçus dans leurs espoirs,se voilent le visage. (14:4).
Even the doe in the field forsakes her newborn fawn because there is no grass (14:5).
The wild donkeys stand on the bare heights; they pant for air like jackals; their eyes fail because there is no vegetation (14:6).
"Though our iniquities testify against us, act, O LORD, for your name's sake; for our backslidings are many; we have sinned against you" (14:7).
O you hope of Israel, its savior in time of trouble, why should you be like a stranger in the land, like a traveler who turns aside to tarry for a night? (14:8).
Why should you be like a man confused, like a mighty warrior who cannot save? Yet you, O LORD, are in the midst of us, and we are called by your name; do not leave us (14:9).

Thus says le SEIGNEUR concerning this people: "They have loved to wander thus; they have not restrained their feet; therefore le SEIGNEUR does not accept them; now he will remember their iniquity and punish their sins" (14:10).
Et l’Eternel me dit : Ne prie pas pour le bien-être de ce peuple ! (14:11).

"Though they fast, I will not hear their cry, and though they offer holocauste and offrande de céréales, I will not accept them. But I will consume them by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence" (14:12).
Then I said: "Ah, Lord GOD, behold, the prophets say to them, 'You shall not see the sword, nor shall you have famine, but I will give you assured peace in this place'" (14:13).

Et l’Eternel me dit : En mon nom, ces prophètes profèrent des mensonges. Je ne les ai pas mandatés, je ne leur ai rien ordonné et je ne leur ai pas parlé : toutes leurs prophéties sont visions mensongères, oracles sans valeur, des inventions venant d’eux-mêmes. (14:14).

Therefore thus says le SEIGNEUR concerning the prophets who prophesy in my name although I did not send them, and who say, "Sword and famine shall not come upon this land": By sword and famine those prophets shall be consumed (14:15).

et les gens du peuple auxquels ils prophétisent seront jetés à terre dans les rues de Jérusalem par la famine et par l’épée, sans qu’il y ait personne pour les mettre au tombeau, ni eux, ni leurs femmes, ni leurs fils, ni leurs filles ; je ferai retomber sur eux le mal qu’ils ont commis. (14:16).
Et toi, dis-leur ceci : (14:17).

If I go out into the field, behold, those pierced by the sword! And if I enter the city, behold, the diseases of famine! For both prophet and priest ply their trade through the land and have no knowledge (14:18).

"Have you utterly rejected Judah? Does your soul loathe Zion? Why have you struck us down so that there is no healing for us? We looked for peace, but no good came; for a time of healing, but behold, terror" (14:19).
We acknowledge our wickedness, O LORD, and the iniquity of our fathers, for we have sinned against you (14:20).
Do not spurn us, for your name's sake; do not dishonor your glorious throne; remember and do not break your covenant with us (14:21).
Are there any among the false gods of the nations that can bring rain? Or can the heavens give showers? Are you not he, O LORD our God? We set our hope on you, for you do all these things (14:22).
crossRefs: Lévitique 26:18-20 — Pluie retenue comme châtiment de l'alliance.
Deutéronome 18:20-22 — Épreuve d'un prophète ; sanction pour la fausse prophétie.
Jérémie 1:18-19 — Promesse initiale de Dieu de faire de Jérémie un mur fortifié.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: חֶרֶב רָעָב וָדֶבֶר (ḥerev, rāʿav, va-dever) — Greek (LXX): μάχαιρα, λιμός, θάνατος/λοιμός — Aramaic (Tg./Syr.): סייפא, כְּפָנָא, מוֹתָנָא
translationNotes.note: Triade de jugement récurrente en Jérémie 14:12.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: נְבִיאֵי הַשֶּׁקֶר (neviʾei ha-sheqer) — Greek (LXX): ψευδοπροφῆται — Aramaic (Tg./Syr.): נביאי דכזבא
translationNotes.note: Ils promettent la sécurité et nient le jugement (14:13-16).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: חוֹמַת נְחֹשֶׁת (ḥomat neḥoshet) — Greek (LXX): τεῖχος χαλκοῦν — Aramaic (Tg.): שוּר דִּנְחָשָׁא
translationNotes.note: Métaphore d'une protection inébranlable pour le prophète (15:20).

stories.keyTakeaway: La sécheresse expose la culpabilité de Juda ; les prophètes menteurs nient le jugement. Dieu annonce l'épée, la famine et la peste, tout en soutenant Son prophète et en promettant de le délivrer.

stories.title: 🌵 Jérémie 15
summaryBullets: Mais l’Eternel me dit : Même si Moïse et Samuel se tenaient devant moi pour prier pour ce peuple, je ne me soucierais pas d’eux. Chasse-le de ma vue, qu’il parte loin de moi ! (15:1).
Et lorsqu’ils te diront : « Où devons-nous aller ? » tu leur diras ceci : (15:2).
Je leur enverrai quatre sortes de maux, déclare l’Eternel : l’épée pour les abattre, les chiens pour les déchirer, les rapaces et les animaux sauvages pour les dévorer et les détruire. (15:3).
"And I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth because of what Manasseh fils de Hezekiah, king of Judah, did in Jerusalem" (15:4).
"Who will have pity on you, O Jerusalem, or who will grieve for you? Who will turn aside to ask about your welfare?" (15:5).
"You have rejected me," declares le SEIGNEUR; "you keep going backward. So I have stretched out my hand against you and destroyed you—I am weary of relenting" (15:6).
Je les ai dispersés ╵aux portes du pays ╵comme par un vannage,j’ai fait périr mon peuple,je l’ai privé d’enfantsparce qu’ils n’abandonnent pas ╵leur mauvaise conduite. (15:7).

"I have made their widows more in number than the sand of the seas; I have brought against the mothers of young men a destroyer at noonday; I have made anguish and terror fall upon them suddenly" (15:8).

La mère de sept fils ╵est misérable ;la voilà haletante,et le soleil ╵s’éteint déjà pour elle ╵avant la fin du jour.La voilà toute honteuse ╵et dans la confusion.Les enfants qui lui restent, ╵je les livre à l’épéedevant leurs ennemis,l’Eternel le déclare. (15:9).
Woe is me, my mother, that you bore me, a man of strife and contention to the whole land! I have not lent, nor have I borrowed, yet all of them curse me (15:10).
L’Eternel répondit :Moi, je t’assure,je te délivrerai ╵pour te faire du bien ;au temps de ton malheur, ╵au temps de ta détresse :ce sont tes ennemis ╵qui viendront t’implorer ! (15:11).
"Can one break iron, iron from the north, and bronze?" (15:12).
"Your wealth and your treasures I will give as spoil, without price, for all your sins, throughout all your territory" (15:13).
"I will make you serve your enemies in a land that you do not know, for in my anger a fire is kindled that shall burn forever" (15:14).
O LORD, you know; remember me and visit me, and take vengeance for me on my persecutors. In your forbearance take me not away; know that for your sake I bear reproach (15:15).
Your words were found, and I ate them, and your words became to me a joy and the delight of my heart, for I am called by your name, O LORD, God of hosts (15:16).
I did not sit in the company of revelers, nor did I rejoice; I sat alone, because your hand was upon me, for you had filled me with indignation (15:17).
Why is my pain unceasing, my wound incurable, refusing to be healed? Will you be to me like a deceitful brook, like waters that fail? (15:18).

Voici la réponse de l’Eternel :Si tu reviens à moi, ╵je te rétablirai.Tu pourras te tenirà mon service.Si ce qui est précieux, ╵tu le sépares ╵de ce qui est indigne,tu seras mon porte-parole.Ils reviendront à toi,mais ce n’est pas à toi ╵de revenir vers eux. (15:19).

"And I will make you to this people a fortified wall of bronze; they will fight against you, but they shall not prevail over you, for I am with you to save you and deliver you," declares le SEIGNEUR (15:20).
Oui, je te délivrerai des méchants,je te sauverai des violents. (15:21).
