stories.title: 🍷 Jérémie 48
summaryBullets: Concerning Moab. Thus says le SEIGNEUR of hosts, the God of Israel: "Woe to Nebo, for it is laid waste! Kiriathaim is put to shame, it is taken; the fortress is put to shame and broken down" (48:1).

The renown of Moab is no more. In Heshbon they planned disaster against her: "Come, let us cut her off from being a nation!" You also, O Madmen, shall be brought to silence; the sword shall pursue you (48:2).
"A voice! A cry from Horonaim, 'Desolation and great destruction!'" (48:3).
Moab is destroyed; her little ones have made a cry (48:4).
For at the ascent of Luhith they go up weeping; for at the descent of Horonaim they have heard the distressed cry of destruction (48:5).
"Flee! Save yourselves! You will be like a juniper in the desert!" (48:6).
For, because you trusted in your works and your treasures, you also shall be taken; and Chemosh shall go into exile with his priests and his officials (48:7).
et le dévastateur ╵fondra sur chaque ville ;non, aucune cité ╵ne sera épargnée.La vallée est ruinée, ╵le plateau ravagé,c’est ce que l’Eternel a dit. (48:8).
"Give wings to Moab, for she would fly away; her cities shall become a desolation, with no inhabitant in them" (48:9).
"Cursed is he who does the work of le SEIGNEUR with slackness, and cursed is he who keeps back his sword from bloodshed" (48:10).

"Moab has been at ease from his youth and has settled on his dregs; he has not been emptied from vessel to vessel, nor has he gone into exile. So his taste remains in him, and his scent is not changed" (48:11).
"Therefore, behold, the days are coming," declares le SEIGNEUR, "when I shall send to him pourers who will pour him, and empty his vessels and break his jars in pieces" (48:12).
Alors Moab, honteux, ╵rougira de Kemoshcomme le peuple d’Israëla rougi de Béthel ╵en qui il se confiait. (48:13).
"How do you say, 'We are heroes and mighty men of war'?" (48:14).
Le dévastateur de Moabvient attaquer ses villes,la fleur de sa jeunesse ╵va tout droit au massacre,c’est là ce que déclare ╵le Roi qui a pour nom : ╵le Seigneur des armées célestes. (48:15).
The calamity of Moab is near at hand, and his affliction hastens swiftly (48:16).
Grieve for him, all you who are around him, and all who know his name; say, "How the mighty scepter is broken, the glorious staff" (48:17).
Descends de ta splendeur,va habiter un lieu aride,ô population de Dibôn,le dévastateur de Moab ╵vient t’attaqueret il détruit tes forteresses. (48:18).
Stand by the road and watch, O inhabitant of Aroer! Ask him who flees and her who escapes; say, "What has happened?" (48:19).
Moab is put to shame, for it is broken; wail and cry! Tell it beside the Arnon, that Moab is laid waste (48:20).
"Judgment has come upon the tableland, upon Holon, and Jahzah, and Mephaath" (48:21),
"and Dibon, and Nebo, and Beth-diblathaim" (48:22),
"and Kiriathaim, and Beth-gamul, and Beth-meon" (48:23),
Voilà que Moab est brisé,et l’on entend les cris ╵de ses petits. (48:24).
The horn of Moab is cut off, and his arm is broken, declares le SEIGNEUR (48:25).
"Make him drunk, because he magnified himself against le SEIGNEUR, so that Moab shall wallow in his vomit, and he too shall be held in derision" (48:26).
"Was not Israel a derision to you? Was he found among thieves, that whenever you spoke of him you wagged your head?" (48:27).
Habitants de Moab,abandonnez les villeset allez demeurer ╵au milieu des rochers !Imitez la colombequi va poser son nid ╵au bord des précipices ! (48:28).
Nous avons entendu parler ╵de l’orgueil de Moab,il est orgueilleux à l’extrême ╵et quel esprit de supériorité !Quelle fierté ! ╵Quelle arrogance !Quel cœur altier ! (48:29).
"I know his insolence," declares le SEIGNEUR; "his boasts are false, his deeds are false" (48:30).
Therefore I wail for Moab; I cry out for all Moab; for the men of Kir-hareseth I mourn (48:31).
More than for Jazer I weep for you, O vine of Sibmah! Your branches passed over the sea, reached to the Sea of Jazer; on your summer fruits and your grapes the destroyer has fallen (48:32).

La joie et l’allégresse ╵ont disparu ╵des vergers de Moabet du pays entier.Je taris le vin dans les cuves,on ne foule plus la vendange ╵avec des cris de joie.C’en est fini ╵des cris de joie ! (48:33).
On entend les cris de Heshbôn ╵jusqu’à Elealé,leur voix s’entend jusqu’à Yahats,de Tsoar à Horonaïmet jusqu’à Eglath-Shelishiya.Les eaux de Nimrim elles-mêmes ╵ont cessé de couler. (48:34).
"And I will bring to an end in Moab," declares le SEIGNEUR, "him who offers sacrifice in the high place and makes offerings to his god" (48:35).
Therefore my heart moans for Moab like a flute, and my heart moans like a flute for the men of Kir-hareseth. Therefore the riches they gained have perished (48:36).
"For every head is shaved and every beard cut off. On all the hands are gashes, and around the waist is sackcloth" (48:37).
On all the housetops of Moab and in the squares there is nothing but lamentation, for I have broken Moab like a vessel for which no one cares, declares le SEIGNEUR (48:38).
"How it is broken! How they wail! How Moab has turned his back in shame! So Moab has become a derision and a horror to all that are around him" (48:39).
For thus says le SEIGNEUR: "Behold, one shall fly swiftly like an eagle and spread his wings against Moab" (48:40).
Qeriyoth est prise,les lieux forts sont conquis,et le cœur des guerriers ╵de Moab, ce jour-là,sera semblable au cœur ╵d’une femme en travail. (48:41).
Moab shall be destroyed and be no longer a people, because he magnified himself against le SEIGNEUR (48:42).
"Terror, pit, and snare are before you, O inhabitant of Moab!" declares le SEIGNEUR (48:43).
Qui s’enfuira devant l’effroitombera dans la fosse,qui remontera de la fossesera pris au filet ;car je ferai venir ╵sur lui, oui, sur Moab,l’année du châtiment,l’Eternel le déclare. (48:44).

A l’ombre de Heshbôn,s’arrêtent des fuyards sans forceparce qu’un feu ╵est sorti de Heshbôn,une flamme a jailli ╵du milieu de Sihônet elle a consumé ╵les tempes de Moabet le crâne des tapageurs. (48:45).
"Woe to you, O Moab! The people of Chemosh are undone, for your sons have been taken captive, and your daughters into captivity" (48:46).
"Yet I will restore the fortunes of Moab in the latter days," declares le SEIGNEUR. Thus far is the judgment on Moab (48:47).
crossRefs: Ésaïe 15-16 — Oracles parallèles contre Moab.
Nombres 21-25 — Moab dans l'histoire d'Israël au désert.
Jérémie 49:39 — Note semblable de restauration « dans les derniers jours » pour Élam.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שָׁקַט הוּא וְשַׁאֲקַט אֶל־שְׁמָרָיו (…el-shemarav) — Greek (LXX): ἐπὶ τῶν οἴνου τρυγῶν — Aramaic (Tg./Syr.): על שמרוהי
translationNotes.note: Vin laissé tranquille sur sa lie : image d'un bien-être non perturbé, désormais bouleversé (48:11).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: נִכְרְתָה קֶרֶן (nikhretah qeren) — Greek (LXX): ἐκόπη κέρας — Aramaic (Tg./Syr.): אתגזרת קרנא
translationNotes.note: Symbole de la force et de la domination supprimées (48:25).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כְּמוֹשׁ (Kemosh) — Greek (LXX): Χαμώς — Aramaic (Tg./Syr.): כמיש
translationNotes.note: Dieu national de Moab, dit partir en exil avec son peuple (48:7).

stories.keyTakeaway: La stabilité, l'orgueil et le vin de Moab sont renversés ; la lamentation monte à travers ses villes, mais une parole finale de restauration est donnée.

stories.title: 🏜️ Jérémie 49
summaryBullets: Concerning the Ammonites. Thus says le SEIGNEUR: "Has Israel no sons? Has he no heir? Why then has Milcom dispossessed Gad, and his people settled in its cities?" (49:1).

C’est pourquoi le temps vient,l’Eternel le déclare,où je ferai entendre ╵les cris de guerre ╵contre Rabba des Ammonites ;elle sera changée ╵en un tertre de ruines,et toutes ses bourgades ╵seront livrées au feu.Israël spolieraceux qui l’auront spolié,l’Eternel le déclare. (49:2).

"Wail, O Heshbon, for Ai is laid waste! Cry out, O daughters of Rabbah! Put on sackcloth, lament, and run to and fro among the hedges! For Milcom shall go into exile, with his priests and his officials" (49:3).
"Why do you boast of your valleys, O faithless daughter, who trusted in her treasures, saying, 'Who will come against me?'" (49:4).

Je fais venir ╵l’épouvante sur toi,de tous tes alentours,l’Eternel le déclare, ╵le Seigneur des armées célestes,et vous serez chassés, ╵chacun droit devant soi,il n’y aura personne ╵qui rassemblera les fuyards. (49:5).
"But afterward I will restore the fortunes of the Ammonites," declares le SEIGNEUR (49:6).
Concerning Edom. Thus says le SEIGNEUR of hosts: "Is wisdom no more in Teman? Has counsel perished from the prudent? Has their wisdom vanished?" (49:7).
"Flee, turn back, dwell in the depths, O inhabitants of Dedan! For I will bring the calamity of Esau upon him, the time when I punish him" (49:8).
"If grape-gatherers came to you, would they not leave gleanings? If thieves came by night, would they not destroy only enough for themselves?" (49:9).
"But I have stripped Esau bare; I have uncovered his hiding places, and he is not able to conceal himself. His children are destroyed, and his brothers, and his neighbors; and he is no more" (49:10).
"Leave your fatherless children; I will keep them alive; and let your widows trust in me" (49:11).
For thus says le SEIGNEUR: "If those who did not deserve to drink the cup must drink it, will you go unpunished? You shall not go unpunished, but you must drink" (49:12).
"For I have sworn by myself," declares le SEIGNEUR, "that Bozrah shall become a horror, a taunt, a waste, and a curse, and all her cities shall be perpetual wastes" (49:13).
I have heard a message from le SEIGNEUR, and an envoy has been sent among the nations: "Gather yourselves together and come against her, and rise up for battle!" (49:14).
"For behold, I will make you small among the nations, despised among mankind" (49:15).

La peur que tu inspires ╵et ton orgueil t’égarent,toi qui as ta demeure ╵dans les creux des rocherset qui occupes ╵le sommet des collines.Oui, comme l’aigle, ╵tu élèves ton nid ;je t’en ferai descendre !l’Eternel le déclare. (49:16).
"Edom shall become a horror. Everyone who passes by it will be horrified and will hiss because of all its disasters" (49:17).
As when Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighboring cities were overthrown, says le SEIGNEUR, no man shall dwell there, no man shall sojourn in her (49:18).

Voici, comme un lion ╵monte des forêts luxuriantes du Jourdainvers des enclos solides,moi, je viendrai ╵les faire déguerpir de là, ╵en un clin d’œil,et je me choisirai ╵quelqu’un pour dominer sur lui.Car qui est mon égal ?Qui me demandera des comptes ?Et quel est le berger ╵qui pourrait tenir contre moi ? (49:19).

Ecoutez donc le plan ╵que l’Eternel a fait ╵contre les Edomites,et les projets qu’il a formés ╵contre la population de Témân :on les entraînera ╵comme les plus chétives ╵des bêtes du troupeauet l’on ravagera ╵après eux leurs enclos. (49:20).
At the sound of their fall the earth shall tremble; the sound of their cry shall be heard at la mer Rouge (49:21).
Ce sera comme un aigle ╵qui monte et plane,et qui étend ses ailes ╵au-dessus de Botsra ;et le cœur des guerriers ╵d’Edom, en ce jour-là,sera semblable au cœur ╵d’une femme en travail. (49:22).
Concerning Damascus. "Hamath and Arpad are confounded, for they have heard bad news; they melt in fear, they are troubled like the sea that cannot be quiet" (49:23).
Damascus has become feeble, she turned to flee, and panic seized her; anguish and sorrows have taken hold of her, as of a woman in labor (49:24).
How is the famous city not forsaken, the city of my joy? (49:25).
Therefore her young men shall fall in her squares, and all her soldiers shall be destroyed in that day, declares le SEIGNEUR of hosts (49:26).
"And I will kindle a fire in the wall of Damascus, and it shall devour the strongholds of Ben-hadad" (49:27).
Prophéties sur Qédar et sur les royaumes de Hatsor vaincus par Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone. (49:28).
Qu’on saisisse leurs tentes ╵et leur petit bétail !Qu’on prenne leurs tapis, ╵tous leurs effets et leurs chameaux !Qu’on proclame contre eux : ╵« De toutes parts, c’est la terreur ! » (49:29).
"Flee, wander far away, dwell in the depths, O inhabitants of Hazor!" declares le SEIGNEUR. "For Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has made a plan against you and formed a purpose against you" (49:30).
"Rise up, advance against a nation at ease, that dwells securely," declares le SEIGNEUR, "that has no gates or bars, that dwells alone" (49:31).

Their camels shall become plunder, their herds of livestock a spoil. I will scatter to every wind those who cut the corners of their hair, and I will bring their calamity from every side of them, declares le SEIGNEUR (49:32).
Hazor shall become a haunt of jackals, an everlasting waste; no man shall dwell there; no man shall sojourn in her (49:33).
Voici le message que l’Eternel adressa au prophète Jérémie au sujet d’Elam, au commencement du règne de Sédécias, roi de Juda : (49:34).
Thus says le SEIGNEUR of hosts: "Behold, I will break the bow of Elam, the mainstay of their might" (49:35).
Je ferai venir sur lui quatre ventsdes quatre coins de l’horizon,et je le disperserai à tous vents.Chez tous les peuples,on verra arriver ╵des fugitifs d’Elam. (49:36).

"I will terrify Elam before their enemies and before those who seek their life. I will bring disaster upon them, my fierce anger," declares le SEIGNEUR. "I will send the sword after them, until I have consumed them" (49:37),
"and I will set my throne in Elam and destroy their king and officials," declares le SEIGNEUR (49:38).
"But in the latter days I will restore the fortunes of Elam," declares le SEIGNEUR (49:39).
crossRefs: Abdias 1 — La chute d'Édom développée.
Amos 1-2 — Oracles contre les voisins (parallèles).
Genèse 14:13 ; Genèse 36:11 — Téman et la lignée édomite.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מִלְכֹּם / מַלְכָּם (Milkōm/Malkam) — Greek (LXX): Μελχὼμ — Aramaic (Tg./Syr.): מלכון
translationNotes.note: Divinité ammonite ou jeu de mots avec « leur roi » ; le texte dit qu'il part en exil (49:1-3).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: תֵּימָן / בָּצְרָה — Greek (LXX): Θαιμὰν / Βοσόρρα — Aramaic (Tg./Syr.): תימן / בצרא
translationNotes.note: Centres édomites visés ; la sagesse de Téman ne sauvera pas (49:7-13).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שִׁבַּרְתִּי אֶת־קֶשֶׁת עֵילָם (shibbarti et-qeshet ‘Elam) — Greek (LXX): συνέτριψα τὸ τόξον Αἰλάμ — Aramaic (Tg./Syr.): תברית קשת עילם
translationNotes.note: La puissance militaire brisée, mais la restauration est promise (49:35-39).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בָּצְרָה (Boṣrāh) — Greek: Βοσόρρα (Bosorra, LXX) — Aramaic: בצרא (Boṣrā)
translationNotes.note: Ville capitale d'Édom.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: בֶּן־הֲדַד (Ben-hădad) — Greek: υἱὸς Ἁδὰδ (huiòs Hadàd, LXX) — Aramaic: בר הדד (Bar-Hadad)
translationNotes.note: Nom dynastique des rois araméens de Damas.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: אַרְבַּע רוּחוֹת (ʾarbaʿ rūḥōt) — Greek: τέσσαρες ἄνεμοι (téssares ánēmoi, LXX) — Aramaic: ארבע רוחות (ʾarbʿ rūḥōt)
translationNotes.note: Symbole de dispersion dans toutes les directions.

stories.keyTakeaway: Le jugement de Dieu frappe Ammon, Édom, Damas, Kédar, Hatsor et Élam par la conquête, l'exil et la destruction. Pourtant la restauration est promise pour Ammon et Élam dans l'avenir.

stories.title: 🧱 Jérémie 50
summaryBullets: Voici le message que l’Eternel communiqua par le prophète Jérémie au sujet de Babylone et du pays des Chaldéens : (50:1).

"Declare among the nations and proclaim, set up a banner and proclaim, do not conceal it, say: 'Babylon is taken, Bel is put to shame, Merodach is dismayed. Her images are put to shame, her idols are dismayed'" (50:2).
"For out of the north a nation has come up against her, which shall make her land a desolation, and none shall dwell in it; both man and beast shall flee away" (50:3).
"In those days and in that time," declares le SEIGNEUR, "les enfants d’Israël and the people of Judah shall come together, weeping as they come, and they shall seek le SEIGNEUR their God" (50:4).
They shall ask the way to Zion, with faces turned toward it, saying, "Come, let us join ourselves to le SEIGNEUR in an everlasting covenant that will never be forgotten" (50:5).
"My people have been lost sheep. Their shepherds have led them astray, turning them away on the mountains. From mountain to hill they have gone. They have forgotten their fold" (50:6).

All who found them have devoured them, and their enemies have said, "We are not guilty, for they have sinned against le SEIGNEUR, their habitation of righteousness, le SEIGNEUR, the hope of their fathers" (50:7).
Partez de Babyloneet du pays des Chaldéens !Oui, sortez-en comme des boucs ╵en tête du troupeau ! (50:8).

Car je vais susciterune coalition ╵de grandes nations des pays du nordpour qu’elles viennent ╵attaquer Babylone.Elles se rangeront ╵en bataille contre elleet s’en empareront.Leurs flèches sont semblables ╵à d’habiles guerrierset elles ne reviennent pas à vide. (50:9).
Et la Chaldée sera mise au pillage ;ceux qui la pilleront ╵se rassasieront bien,l’Eternel le déclare. (50:10).
"Though you rejoice, though you exult, O plunderers of my heritage, though you frolic like a heifer in the pasture, and neigh like stallions" (50:11),

votre mère-patrie ╵est toute couverte de honte,celle qui vous a enfantés ╵connaît le déshonneur.La voici mise au dernier rang ╵de toutes les nations,devenue un désert, ╵une terre aride, une steppe. (50:12).

L’indignation de l’Eternelen a fait une terre ╵où tout est dévastéet où personne n’habite.Tous ceux qui passeront ╵tout près de Babyloneen seront effarés ╵et siffleront d’horreur ╵à la vue de toutes ses plaies. (50:13).
"Set yourselves in array against Babylon all around, all you who bend the bow; shoot at her, spare no arrows, for she has sinned against le SEIGNEUR" (50:14).

Raise a shout against her all around; she has surrendered; her bulwarks have fallen; her walls are thrown down. For this is the vengeance of le SEIGNEUR: take vengeance on her; do to her as she has done (50:15).

Eliminez de Babylone ╵à la fois le semeuret celui qui tient la faucille ╵au temps de la moisson !Et devant l’épée meurtrière,chacun s’en retournera chez les siens,chacun fuira dans son pays ! (50:16).
"Israel is a hunted sheep driven away by lions. First the king of Assyria devoured him, and now at last Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has gnawed his bones" (50:17).
Et c’est pourquoi ╵voici ce que déclare ╵le Seigneur des armées célestes, ╵Dieu d’Israël :Je vais rétribuer ╵le roi de Babylone ╵et son pays,tout comme j’ai rétribué ╵le roi de l’Assyrie. (50:18).
"I will restore Israel to his pasture, and he shall feed on Carmel and in Bashan, and his desire shall be satisfied on the hills of Ephraim and in Gilead" (50:19).

En ce temps-là, ╵à cette époque,l’Eternel le déclare,on aura beau chercher ╵la faute d’Israël,elle aura disparu,le péché de Juda,on ne le retrouvera plus ;car je pardonnerai au reste ╵que j’aurai épargné. (50:20).
"Go up against the land of Merathaim, and against the inhabitants of Pekod. Kill, and devote them to destruction," declares le SEIGNEUR, "and do all that I have commanded you" (50:21).
The noise of battle is in the land, and great destruction! (50:22).
How the hammer of the whole earth is cut down and broken! How Babylon has become a horror among the nations! (50:23).
I set a snare for you and you were taken, O Babylon, and you did not know it; you were found and caught, because you opposed le SEIGNEUR (50:24).
L’Eternel a ouvert son arsenalet il en a tiré les armes ╵de sa colère ;car c’est là l’œuvreque l’Eternel, ╵le Seigneur des armées célestes, ╵va accomplirdans le pays des Chaldéens. (50:25).
Come against her from every quarter; open her granaries; pile her up like heaps of grain, and devote her to destruction; let nothing be left of her (50:26).
Kill all her bulls; let them go down to the slaughter. Woe to them, for their day has come, the time of their punishment (50:27).
A voice! They flee and escape from the land of Babylon, to declare in Zion the vengeance of le SEIGNEUR our God, vengeance for his temple (50:28).

"Summon archers against Babylon, all those who bend the bow. Encamp around her; let no one escape. Repay her according to her deeds; do to her according to all that she has done. For she has proudly defied le SEIGNEUR, the Holy One of Israel" (50:29).
Therefore her young men shall fall in her squares, and all her soldiers shall be destroyed on that day, declares le SEIGNEUR (50:30).
"Behold, I am against you, O proud one," declares the Lord GOD of hosts, "for your day has come, the time when I will punish you" (50:31).
The proud one shall stumble and fall, with none to raise him up, and I will kindle a fire in his cities, and it will devour all that is around him (50:32).
Thus says le SEIGNEUR of hosts: "The enfants d’Israël are oppressed, and the people of Judah with them. All who took them captive have held them fast; they refuse to let them go" (50:33).

Pourtant, leur libérateur est puissant :oui il se nomme ╵le Seigneur des armées célestes.Il prend en main leur cause ╵et il la défendra.Il donnera ╵la tranquillité au payset il ébranlera ╵les habitants de Babylone. (50:34).
"A sword against the Chaldeans," declares le SEIGNEUR, "and against the inhabitants of Babylon, and against her officials and her wise men!" (50:35).
A sword against the diviners, that they may become fools! A sword against her warriors, that they may be destroyed! (50:36).

A sword against her horses and against her chariots, and against all the foreign troops in her midst, that they may become women! A sword against all her treasures, that they may be plundered! (50:37).
A drought against her waters, that they may be dried up! For it is a land of images, and they are mad over idols (50:38).
"Therefore wild beasts shall dwell with hyenas in Babylon, and ostriches shall dwell in her. She shall never again have people, nor be inhabited for all generations" (50:39).
As when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighboring cities, declares le SEIGNEUR, so no man shall dwell there, and no son of man shall sojourn in her (50:40).
Un peuple va venir du nord,une grande nation ; ╵des rois nombreuxse mettent en campagne ╵des confins de la terre. (50:41).

They lay hold of bow and spear; they are cruel and have no mercy. The sound of them is like the roaring of the sea; they ride on horses, arrayed as a man for battle against you, O daughter of Babylon! (50:42).
"The king of Babylon heard the report of them, and his hands fell helpless; anguish seized him, pain as of a woman in labor" (50:43).

Voici, comme un lion ╵monte des forêts luxuriantes du Jourdainvers des enclos solides,moi je viendrai ╵les faire déguerpir de là ╵en un clin d’œil,et je me choisirai ╵quelqu’un pour dominer sur lui.Car qui est mon égal ?Qui me demandera des comptes ?Et quel est le berger ╵qui pourrait tenir contre moi ? (50:44).

Ecoutez donc le plan ╵que l’Eternel ╵a formé contre Babylone,et les projets qu’il a formés ╵au sujet du pays des Chaldéens :on les entraînera ╵comme les plus chétives ╵des bêtes du troupeauet l’on ravagera ╵après eux leur enclos. (50:45).
Au bruit de la prise de Babylone,la terre tremblera,et chez les peuples étrangers, ╵on entendra un cri. (50:46).
crossRefs: Ésaïe 13:1 ; Ésaïe 14:1 — Oracles contre Babylone.
Apocalypse 18:1 — Chute de « Babylone » dans une vision ultérieure.
Jérémie 25:26 — « Shéshac » utilisé comme chiffre pour Babylone.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מְרַתַּיִם (‘double rebellion’), פְּקוֹד (‘punishment/visitation’) — Greek (LXX): Μαραθαΐμ / Φεκώδ — Aramaic (Tg./Syr.): מראתים / פקוד
translationNotes.note: Jeux de mots délibérés sur des cibles de jugement (50:21) (51:1).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: תַּנִּינִים (tannînîm) — Greek (LXX): δράκοντες (drakontes)
translationNotes.note: Signifie souvent serpent, monstre marin ou dragon ; ici utilisé au sujet de Nebucadnetsar dévorant Jérusalem et les nations.

stories.keyTakeaway: Babylone est condamnée pour son orgueil et pour avoir détruit le temple de Dieu. Le peuple est sommé de fuir ; un rouleau est coulé dans le fleuve en signe que Babylone tombera et ne se relèvera pas.

stories.title: 🧱 Jérémie 51
summaryBullets: Thus says le SEIGNEUR: "Behold, I will stir up the spirit of a destroyer against Babylon, against the inhabitants of Leb-kamai" (51:1),
"and I will send to Babylon winnowers, and they shall winnow her, and they shall empty her land, when they come against her from every side on the day of trouble" (51:2).
Let not the archer bend his bow, and let him not stand up in his armor. Spare not her young men; devote to destruction all her army (51:3).
Ceux qui seront frappés à mort ╵joncheront le pays des Chaldéens,les blessés tomberont ╵dans les rues de la ville. (51:4).

Bien que leur pays soit souillé ╵d’offenses à l’égarddu Dieu saint d’Israël,la terre d’Israël ╵et celle de Juda ╵n’ont pas été abandonnées ╵au veuvage par l’Eternel,le Seigneur des armées célestes. (51:5).
"Flee from the midst of Babylon; let every one save his life! Be not cut off in her punishment, for this is the time of le SEIGNEUR's vengeance, the repayment he is rendering her" (51:6).
Babylon was a golden cup in le SEIGNEUR's hand, making all the earth drunken; the nations drank of her wine; therefore the nations went mad (51:7).
Suddenly Babylon has fallen and been broken; wail for her! Take balm for her pain; perhaps she may be healed (51:8).
We would have healed Babylon, but she was not healed. Forsake her, and let us go each to his own country, for her judgment has reached up to heaven and has been lifted up even to the skies (51:9).
The LORD has brought about our vindication; come, let us declare in Zion the work of le SEIGNEUR our God (51:10).

Aiguisez bien les flèches,prenez vos boucliers !L’Eternel a excité ╵l’esprit des rois des Mèdes,car il a résolu ╵de ruiner Babylone ;ce sera la rétribution, ╵que l’Eternel exercera,ainsi il lui fera payer ╵ce qu’elle a fait contre son temple. (51:11).

Set up a standard against the walls of Babylon; make the watch strong; set up watchmen; prepare the ambushes; for le SEIGNEUR has both planned and done what he spoke concerning the inhabitants of Babylon (51:12).
O you who dwell by many waters, rich in treasures, your end has come; the thread of your life is cut (51:13).
The LORD of hosts has sworn by himself: "Surely I will fill you with men, as many as locusts, and they shall raise the shout of victory over you" (51:14).
It is he who made the earth by his power, who established the world by his wisdom, and by his understanding stretched out the heavens (51:15).

Quand il fait retentir sa voix,des torrents d’eau ╵s’amassent dans le ciel ;des nuages s’élèvent ╵des confins de la terre ;il fait jaillir l’éclair ╵au milieu des averseset il fait s’élancer ╵le vent de ses réserves. (51:16).
Every man is stupid and without knowledge; every goldsmith is put to shame by his idols, for his images are false, and there is no breath in them (51:17).
They are worthless, a work of delusion; at the time of their punishment they shall perish (51:18).
Not like these is he who is the portion of Jacob, for he is the one who formed all things, and Israel is la tribu de his inheritance; le SEIGNEUR of hosts is his name (51:19).
"You are my hammer and weapon of war: with you I break nations in pieces; with you I destroy kingdoms" (51:20);
"with you I break in pieces the horse and his rider; with you I break in pieces the chariot and the charioteer" (51:21);
Par toi, j’ai pilonné ╵des hommes et des femmes.Par toi, j’ai pilonné ╵des vieillards, des enfants.Par toi, j’ai pilonné ╵des jeunes hommes, ╵des jeunes filles. (51:22).
"with you I break in pieces the shepherd and his flock; with you I break in pieces the farmer and his team; with you I break in pieces governors and commanders" (51:23).
"I will repay Babylon and all the inhabitants of Chaldea before your very eyes for all the evil that they have done in Zion," declares le SEIGNEUR (51:24).

"Behold, I am against you, O destroying mountain," declares le SEIGNEUR, "which destroys the whole earth; I will stretch out my hand against you, and roll you down from the crags, and make you a burnt mountain" (51:25).
et l’on ne prendra plus ╵de toi ni pierre d’angleni pierres pour les fondations ;car tu seras ╵pour toujours dévastée,l’Eternel le déclare. (51:26).

"Set up a standard on the earth; blow the trumpet among the nations; prepare the nations for war against her; summon against her the kingdoms, Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz; appoint a marshal against her; bring up horses like bristling locusts" (51:27).
Prepare the nations for war against her, the kings of the Medes, with their governors and deputies, and every land under their dominion (51:28).
La terre est ébranlée, ╵elle vacille,car les desseins que l’Eternel ╵a conçus contre Babylone ╵se réalisentpour changer son pays ╵en une terre dévastée ╵et privée d’habitants. (51:29).
The warriors of Babylon have ceased fighting; they remain in their strongholds; their strength has failed; they have become women; her dwellings are on fire; her bars are broken (51:30).
One runner runs to meet another, and one messenger to meet another, to tell the king of Babylon that his city is taken on every side (51:31);
the fords have been seized, the marshes are burned with fire, and the soldiers are in panic (51:32).

For thus says le SEIGNEUR of hosts, the God of Israel: "The daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time when it is trodden; yet a little while and the time of her harvest will come" (51:33).

Nabuchodonosor, ╵le roi de Babylone,nous a dévorés, ╵nous a mis en déroute,et il nous a laissés ╵comme un récipient vide.Il nous a engloutis ╵tout comme un monstre.Il a rempli son ventre ╵du meilleur de nous-mêmes,puis il nous a bannis. (51:34).
"The violence done to me and to my kinsmen be upon Babylon," let the inhabitant of Zion say. "My blood be upon the inhabitants of Chaldea," let Jerusalem say (51:35).
Therefore thus says le SEIGNEUR: "Behold, I will plead your cause and take vengeance for you. I will dry up her sea and make her fountain dry" (51:36),
"and Babylon shall become a heap of ruins, the haunt of jackals, a horror and a hissing, without inhabitant" (51:37).
They shall roar together like lions; they shall growl like lions' cubs (51:38).
"While they are inflamed I will prepare them a feast and make them drunk, that they may become merry, then sleep a perpetual sleep and not wake," declares le SEIGNEUR (51:39).
"I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams and boucs" (51:40).
"How Babylon is taken, the praise of the whole earth seized! How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!" (51:41).
The sea has come up on Babylon; she is covered with its tumultuous waves (51:42).
Her cities have become a horror, a land of drought and a desert, a land in which no one dwells, and through which no son of man passes (51:43).
"And I will punish Bel in Babylon, and take out of his mouth what he has swallowed. The nations shall no longer flow to him; the wall of Babylon has fallen" (51:44).
Sortez du milieu d’elle, ╵vous, membres de mon peuple !Et que chacun sauve sa viequand la colère ardente ╵de l’Eternel se manifestera ! (51:45).

Mais faites attention : ╵ne perdez pas courage,ne vous effrayez pasdes rumeurs qui circulent ╵à travers le pays !Une année, court tel bruit ;l’année suivante, un autre,la violence sévit dans le pays,un despote s’en prend ╵à un autre despote. (51:46).
C’est pourquoi, le temps vientoù moi j’interviendrai ╵contre les idoles de Babylone.Son pays tout entier ╵en sera dans la honte,tous ses blessés à mort ╵tomberont au beau milieu d’elle. (51:47).
Le ciel comme la terreet tout ce qu’ils renfermentexulteront de joie ╵devant le sort de Babylone,car du septentrion ╵des destructeurs viennent contre elle,l’Eternel le déclare. (51:48).
Babylon must fall for the slain of Israel, just as for Babylon have fallen the slain of all the earth (51:49).
"You who have escaped the sword, go, do not stand still! Remember le SEIGNEUR from far away, and let Jerusalem come into your mind" (51:50).
"We are put to shame, for we have heard reproach; dishonor has covered our face, for foreigners have come into the holy places of le SEIGNEUR's house" (51:51).
"Therefore, behold, the days are coming," declares le SEIGNEUR, "when I will execute judgment upon her images, and through all her land the wounded shall groan" (51:52).
Though Babylon should mount up to heaven, and though she should fortify her strong height, yet destroyers would come from me against her, declares le SEIGNEUR (51:53).
Un cri se fait entendre, ╵venant de Babylone,le bruit d’un immense désastre ╵retentit en Chaldée. (51:54).
For le SEIGNEUR is laying Babylon waste and stilling her mighty voice. Their waves roar like many waters; the noise of their voice is raised (51:55),
for a destroyer has come upon her, upon Babylon; her warriors are taken; their bows are broken in pieces, for le SEIGNEUR is a God of recompense; he will surely repay (51:56).

"I will make drunk her officials and her wise men, her governors, her commanders, and her warriors; they shall sleep a perpetual sleep and not wake," declares the King, whose name is le SEIGNEUR of hosts (51:57).

Voici ce que déclare ╵le Seigneur des armées célestes :Les larges murs de Babyloneseront démantelés ;ses hautes portes ╵seront la proie des flammes.Les peuples travaillent pour rien,les nations se fatiguent ╵pour ce qui périt par le feu. (51:58).

Voici les instructions que le prophète Jérémie donna à Seraya, fils de Nériya, petit-fils de Mahséya, et responsable du campement, lorsque celui-ci se rendit à Babylone avec Sédécias, roi de Juda, la quatrième année de son règne. (51:59).
Jeremiah wrote in a book all the disaster that should come upon Babylon, all these words that are written concerning Babylon (51:60).
And Jeremiah said to Seraiah: "When you come to Babylon, see that you read all these words" (51:61),
"and say, 'O LORD, you have said concerning this place that you will cut it off, so that nothing shall dwell in it, neither man nor beast, and it shall be desolate forever'" (51:62).
"When you finish reading this book, tie a stone to it and cast it into the midst of the Euphrates" (51:63),
"and say, 'Thus shall Babylon sink, to rise no more, because of the disaster that I am bringing upon her, and they shall become exhausted.'" Thus far are the words of Jeremiah (51:64).

stories.title: 🏚️ Jérémie 52
summaryBullets: Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah (52:1).
And he did what was evil in the sight of le SEIGNEUR, according to all that Jehoiakim had done (52:2).
Tout cela arriva parce que l’Eternel était en colère contre Jérusalem et Juda, au point de les chasser loin de lui. (52:3).

La neuvième année de son règne, le dixième jour du dixième mois, Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, vint avec toute son armée attaquer Jérusalem. Ils établirent leur camp devant la ville et construisirent des terrassements tout autour. (52:4).
So the city was besieged till the eleventh year of King Zedekiah (52:5).
Le neuvième jour du quatrième mois, alors que la famine sévissait durement dans la ville et que la population du pays n’avait plus rien à manger, (52:6).

une brèche fut ouverte dans le rempart de la ville et tous les soldats de Juda s’enfuirent : ils s’échappèrent de la ville, de nuit, par la porte qui se trouvait entre les deux remparts et qui donnait sur le jardin du roi, tandis que la ville était encerclée par les Chaldéens, et ils prirent le chemin de la vallée du Jourdain. (52:7).
Mais l’armée des Chaldéens se lança à la poursuite du roi, et rattrapa Sédécias dans la plaine de Jéricho. Alors tous ses soldats se dispersèrent loin de lui. (52:8).
Les Chaldéens se saisirent du roi et l’amenèrent au roi de Babylone à Ribla, dans le pays de Hamath, et celui-ci prononça son jugement contre lui. (52:9).
The king of Babylon slaughtered les fils de Zedekiah before his eyes, and also slaughtered all the officials of Judah at Riblah (52:10).
He put out the eyes of Zedekiah, and bound him in chains, and the king of Babylon took him to Babylon, and put him in prison till the day of his death (52:11).

Le dixième jour du cinquième mois – c’était la dix-neuvième année du règne de Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone – Nebouzaradân, chef de la garde impériale qui était attaché au service personnel du roi de Babylone, fit son entrée à Jérusalem. (52:12).
Il mit le feu au temple de l’Eternel, au palais royal, à toutes les maisons et à tous les édifices importants de la ville. (52:13).
Les troupes chaldéennes, sous le commandement du chef de la garde, démantelèrent les remparts qui entouraient la ville. (52:14).

Nebouzaradân, chef de la garde impériale, déporta une partie des gens les plus pauvres et le reste de la population qui était demeurée dans la ville, ceux qui s’étaient déjà rendus au roi de Babylone et ce qui restait des artisans. (52:15).
Mais il laissa une partie des gens pauvres du pays pour cultiver les vignes et les champs. (52:16).

Les Chaldéens mirent en pièces les colonnes de bronze du temple de l’Eternel, les chariots et la grande cuve de bronze qui étaient dans le parvis du Temple, et ils emportèrent tout le bronze à Babylone. (52:17).
Ils prirent aussi les chaudrons, les pelles, les couteaux, les coupes à aspersion, les autres coupes et tous les autres objets de bronze employés pour le culte. (52:18).
Le chef de la garde s’empara de tous les objets d’or et d’argent massif : les bassins, les brasiers, les coupes à aspersion, les chaudrons, les chandeliers, les autres coupes et les bols. (52:19).

On ne saurait évaluer le poids du bronze des deux colonnes, de la grande cuve et des douze bœufs de bronze qui soutenaient les chariots, que le roi Salomon avait fait faire pour le temple de l’Eternel. (52:20).
Chaque colonne avait neuf mètres de haut, sa circonférence était de six mètres, le bronze avait près de huit centimètres d’épaisseur, la colonne étant creuse à l’intérieur. (52:21).
Elle était surmontée d’un chapiteau de bronze de deux mètres cinquante de haut, entouré d’un treillis décoré de grenades. Le tout était en bronze. (52:22).
There were ninety-six pomegranates on the sides; all the pomegranates were a hundred upon the network all around (52:23).
Le chef de la garde fit prisonnier le grand-prêtre Seraya, Sophonie, le prêtre en second, et les trois prêtres chargés de surveiller l’entrée du Temple. (52:24).

Il arrêta aussi, dans la ville, un haut responsable militaire, sept conseillers du roi, qui étaient restés dans la ville, le secrétaire du chef de l’armée chargé de recruter les soldats dans le pays, ainsi que soixante Judéens qui se trouvaient à l’intérieur de la ville. (52:25).
Nebouzaradân, chef de la garde, emmena tous ces prisonniers au roi de Babylone, à Ribla. (52:26).
Celui-ci les fit exécuter à Ribla, dans le pays de Hamath. Ainsi, la population de Juda fut déportée loin de sa patrie. (52:27).
Voici le nombre des captifs que Nabuchodonosor emmena en exil : 3 023 Judéens, la septième année de son règne : (52:28).
in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar he carried away captive from Jerusalem 832 persons (52:29);
Puis, la vingt-troisième année du règne de Nabuchodonosor, Nebouzaradân, le chef de la garde, déporta encore 745 Judéens ; ce qui donne un total de 4 600 déportés. (52:30).

La trente-septième année de la déportation de Yehoyakîn, roi de Juda, le vingt-cinquième jour du douzième mois, Evil-Merodak, roi de Babylone, gracia Yehoyakîn, roi de Juda, l’année de son accession au trône de Babylone, et le fit sortir de prison. (52:31).
Il le traita avec bonté et lui accorda une situation supérieure à celle des autres rois exilés avec lui à Babylone. (52:32).
So Jehoiachin put off his prison garments. And every day of his life he dined regularly at the king's table (52:33).
And for his allowance, a regular allowance was given him by the king of Babylon, a portion for each day until the day of his death, all the days of his life (52:34).
